blocks.text: Sunday School Material for Adults 1
L ESSO N 1
THE TRANSFIGURATION OF JESUS
Scripture Text: Luke 9:28-36

In our study of the life of Christ and His work here on earth, we are looking at Him as existing in past eternity and in future eternity as well as the brief time He spent on earth. We have seen Him creating the universe with His Father and the Holy Spirit, appearing on earth before His birth here, promised to be sent to earth, and becoming human and living among men. Now we come to the third and last year of His ministry. His unchanging separation from, and denunciation of, evil has brought the enmity and rejection of the masses to whom He had shown the power of God. He also won the devoted loyalty of a few. Compare Mark 9:2-9 and Matthew 17:1-13.
MEMORY VERSE: And there came a voice out of the cloud, saying, This is my beloved Son: hear him. Luke 9:35
Christ Transfigured

Luke 9:28-29 Jesus took Peter and John and James, and went up into a mountain to pray. He wanted them alone for the sacred scene to follow. Nothing like this had the eyes of man ever seen. It was too sacred for most to see; these three great men could not handle it. They went to sleep while Jesus prayed. And as He prayed, the fashion of his countenance was altered, and his raiment was white and glistering–A brighter scene than earth affords, strange indeed. Jesus was changed. The glory of God shone through His human body. The veil put on Him for His earthly stay was removed and showed briefly His inner glory, His true nature, and gave a glimpse of what God is really like. God was honoring Him. The manifestation of God was so strong that it overflowed into the material of His clothing.
Two Men Brought Back

Luke 9:30-31 Equally as miraculous as the change in Jesus was the bringing back of Moses and Elias (Elijah) from the other world. There talked with Him two men . . . Moses and Elias. Moses was the great leader through whom God gave the Law to Israel. He represents the dispensation of the Law. He died in 1451 B.C. Elias, one of the greatest of the Prophets, represents God's government by the Prophets (1 Kings, Chapters 17, 18, 19, and 21). He was translated some 925 years before; yet here they were living and talking. They were examples of the everlasting life Jesus talked about. Once begun, no life ever ends. They were talking with Jesus of his decease which he should accomplish at Jerusalem.

The Law with its forms and sacrifices pointed forward to Christ (Galatians 3:24). All of its types were fulfilled in Jesus. The Prophets also pointed forward to Christ. His coming and salvation fulfilled their predictions. They talked of Christ's death because it was the finish of the work in whose beginning they had so vital a part. God brought these representatives of the Law and the Prophets back to hear from Christ Himself the plan for the glorious finish of the program so long awaited by them. This was the climax of the purpose for which He came to earth.

Sunday School Material for Adults 2
God Drives Away Confusion

Luke 9:32-33 But Peter and they . . . were heavy with sleep: and when they were awake, they saw . . . It is marvelous what God can show us if He can only get us awake. Peter said . . . quick-speaking Peter, usually too quick–good for us to be here. What great company they were in; Peter wanted to stay there. Let us make three tabernacles, one for thee . . . Moses . . . Elias: not knowing what he said. A great idea, but a man's idea. This is where confusion begins. Every time men's ideas get them to believe that great men are equal to Jesus, they want to build tabernacles to them, and more confusion is added to the minds of the people.

Luke 9:34 While he thus spake–God stops this kind of business very quickly. This was connected with Heaven. His appearance was such as no earthly power could produce. Citizens of Heaven came for the occasion and a voice from Heaven took part in it. Matthew 17:6 tells us they fell on their face, and were sore afraid. No wonder they were afraid! Peter's words had caused a cloud to be placed over the whole wonderful scene. Where once they could see plainly now a cloud had blinded their sight.

Luke 9:35 Voice out of the cloud, saying, This is my beloved Son: hear him. The Law and the Prophets are not our guides now. Only Jesus Christ is to be obeyed. He is the Head of all things. The Voice of God named Jesus His Son as the One to be heard and obeyed. Hear him. In these two words is the solution for the division and confusion in the religious world, for all false doctrines, and for all the evils and troubles of the world today.
See Jesus Only

Luke 9:36 Jesus was found alone. When the Voice of God was past, they saw no one else but Jesus. Jesus told them to tell the vision to no man (Matthew 17:8-9). The vision was over. Jesus commanded secrecy concerning this until after He was risen again from the dead. Jesus did not want them to tell about visions. He wanted them to tell the Gospel. They did not understand and Jesus did not want them to speak that which they did not understand. After His death they would be given understanding of all things by the Holy Spirit. His rising would be the greatest proof of His Deity.
JUST A THOUGHT
"The only test of fellowship is the existence of fellowship." – D.S. Warner

JESUS' RAISING OF LAZARUS
Scripture Text: John 11:1-44

Today we find Jesus in contact with the home of Lazarus, Mary, and Martha. Lazarus is sick unto death, and the sisters send to Jesus an urgent message. It was amazing to the sisters that Jesus made no immediate response to their call in behalf of their brother. When Jesus finally arrived at Bethany, Martha met Him with much sorrow. She said, "Lord if thou hadst been here, my brother had not died." Jesus replied, "I am the resurrection, and the life: he that believeth in me, though he were dead, yet shall he live." Jesus did not say that resurrection came about through Him. He said, "I AM the resurrection, and the life."
MEMORY VERSE: Jesus said unto her, I am the resurrection, and the life: he that believeth in me, though he were dead, yet shall he live. John 11:25
Death of Lazarus

John 11:1-17 A certain man was sick . . . Lazarus . . . Mary and her sister Martha. This event occurred just before Jesus entered Jerusalem for the last week before His crucifixion–a very busy week before He faced the Cross. It seemed amazing to the sisters–as it would to us until we read the complete story through–that Jesus was in no hurry to go to them. Here we see an example of those strange delays of the divine which so often bewilder us. But within these delays are wrapped some of God's richest blessings. It is hard to see how such a misfortune can be for the glory of God. It was not fear of the Jews that kept Him away, such as His disciples felt for Him (verse 8). Jesus' actions were planned. He lived as continual Master of every situation. He saw the end from the beginning.

Lazarus is dead. How did Jesus know? No messenger had come to Him. I am glad . . . I was not there–Let the situation be at its worst, that the remedy may appear more clearly. To the intent ye may believe–To inspire belief is the purpose in Jesus' mind. In the grave four days–No question that he is dead, beyond human help.
Jesus Is the Resurrection

John 11:18-37 When Jesus came, Martha met Him outside the village. There is faith and also a tone of rebuke in her words–Lord, if thou hadst been here, my brother had not died. She questioned in her mind why He hadn't come immediately. But I know, that even now . . . She thought this a harder case than illness, but had hope in Jesus' ability. Is anything too hard for Him who can do all things? When Jesus told her, Thy brother shall rise again, she thought He spoke of the future Resurrection.

I am the resurrection, and the life–Jesus Christ holds the power of life. He has even more, He IS life. He that believeth in me, though he were dead, yet shall he live–life in soul and life in body. Jesus gives life to both. Both are resurrections, the soul being made alive spiritually and the body being made alive after death. Whosoever liveth–is born again, made alive spiritually–and believeth in me–continues joined to Him by faith–shall never die–the second death, eternal spiritual death cannot touch him (Revelation 20:14). There will be a resurrection of the body on some distant day, but for everyone who accepts Jesus as Lord and Savior, there is an immediate resurrection from sin to salvation, from darkness to light, from bondage to freedom, from death

into a life that is everlasting. Believest thou this? She saith unto him, Yea, Lord. Martha's faith reached far enough. Her mind may not have comprehended all, but in taking Him in, she took in all He could do and would do. Jesus wept. At the grave of Lazarus we see Jesus sharing human sorrow. He continues to share it to this very hour. "Does Jesus care? . . . Oh, yes, He cares, I know He cares, His heart is touched with my grief . . . I know my Savior cares." Thank God for a caring Jesus!
Lazarus Resurrected

John 11:38-44 Jesus . . . groaning in himself–grieved and burdened. Take ye away the stone. When Jesus Himself was raised from the dead, angels rolled back the stone from the door of the tomb. But on this occasion Jesus refused to use divine power so long as there was human power available and unused. He commanded human beings to roll back the stone. When man is involved, God will give him a part to do. God will not do for us what we can do for ourselves. Martha thought of the immediate problem–he stinketh. There was a weakness in her faith. Jesus tried to help it–if thou wouldest believe, thou shouldest see . . . We have many stones to roll aside to get our faith where it needs to be to receive miracles from God. Some are the stones of unbelief, doubt, and anxiety. Jesus lifted up his eyes–All His work was in close relationship with His Father. Thou hearest me always–never a break in their fellowship, nothing to hinder His prayers. This is how WE fulfill the Scripture, "Pray without ceasing" (1 Thessalonians 5:17). Broken fellowship with God brings a hindrance in our prayers. This union with God is the secret of victory and prayer answers for us as well as for Jesus. Because of the people which stand by I said it. The concern of Jesus was always for the people around Him. That they may believe that thou hast sent me. Here we see from Jesus' words how important it is that we believe this–for if ye believe not that I am he, ye shall die in your sins (John 8:24).

He cried . . . Lazarus, come forth. And he that was dead came forth. By His Word Jesus had power over death. Lazarus was not raised to life as we will be on the Resurrection Day. He had to die again. Then we all will be changed and made immortal, to die no more. Christ was the first to experience this change to His body (1 Corinthians 15:20). Loose him, and let him go. Now was complete the purpose for which He had acted as He had. The faith of the sisters was honored, many believers were added, the disciples were anchored stronger in faith, and God and His Son were glorified. Lazarus was bound with graveclothes, and his face was bound about with a napkin when he came forth. Even after men are saved, they need the help of others in order to break many of the binding powers that sin had placed upon them. It is our duty, as saints, to help to loose them and let them go free.
God's Will

How many of our misfortunes would be for the glory of God if we only let Him finish what He has begun? This is His plan for giving us blessing. God can use even sickness and death to our good and His glory if we hold onto Him in faith and let Him follow out His purpose.
JUST A THOUGHT
The promises of God are certain, but they do not all mature in ninety days.

JESUS ENTERS JERUSALEM
Scripture Text: Matthew 21:1-11

It is Passover time in Jerusalem. Thousands of pilgrims are traveling to the city for the yearly feast and worship. One among them, Jesus Christ of Nazareth, has a greater purpose. He is coming to die. The journey to Jerusalem was almost finished. Jesus and the disciples climbed the slope of the Mount of Olives. Jesus knew a donkey and her colt were tied in Bethany, and He sent two disciples to bring them. They were not proud horses of war but lowly donkeys of peace and service. This was a fulfillment of prophecy.
MEMORY VERSE: And if any man say aught unto you, ye shall say, The Lord hath need of them; and straightway he will send them. Matthew 21:3
Finding the Colt

Matthew 21:1-3 Coming from Jericho, Jesus and His disciples retreat to the slope of Olivet. Close by is the village of Bethphage. Two disciples are sent to bring from Bethphage an ass tied, and a colt with her. It was an unbroken colt whereon never man sat. On this eventful day the Lord had need of something. He, the King of the universe, had to borrow the colt of a lowly donkey to ride into Jerusalem in triumph. Jesus knew this trip to Jerusalem meant suffering and death. Let us never think of Him as one who was pursued by His enemies and at last overtaken and brought to wicked judgment. He faced the tragic facts of life and walked toward them. The only answer these disciples were to give was The Lord hath need of them. Jesus did not require much from the villager who owned the animal, but He required what the man had. The Lord today has needs; He needs what WE have. Nothing is too lowly to be used in His service. Herod had nothing to contribute on that day, neither had the Roman Emperor. But the humble villager who had a donkey's colt did have something the Lord needed, and he was willing to give it for the cause of Christ. What might our reaction be if someone walked into our driveway and began to drive our automobile away and the only reply we received from him was that the Lord had need of it?
Prophecy Fulfilled

Matthew 21:4-9 All this was done, that it might be fulfilled . . . thy King cometh . . . This whole thing was the fulfillment of Zechariah's prophecy (Zechariah 9:9-10). For this purpose Jesus came into the world. Pomp and ceremony mark the doings of earthly kings. Here the King of kings advanced to His death. He owned the cattle on a thousand hills, yet borrowed, not a horse of war, but a lowly donkey of peace and service. It was unbroken, yet miraculously responded to Jesus' control at a time when the happenings around the animal were such as to cause it to be completely out of control.

A very great multitude–Many gathered because of the miracles Jesus had performed along the way. They came from Jerusalem to meet the One who raised the dead and opened the blind eyes. Spread their garments in the way–branches from the trees–honoring Jesus. The crowds waved palm branches, gathered twigs from the trees, and made from these and their own garments a carpet over which Jesus could ride. No wonder the donkey stayed calm through all of this. Here was Heaven's King riding on his back over earth's highways. The Jews had sought to stone Him, yet He fearlessly let all see Him come. He rides to His death but weeps for His rejecters. He owns all yet

shows no pride. He is King yet has no adornments.

This was unplanned by man but certainly planned by God. He told His prophets of it hundreds of years before. Fulfillment of prophecy is proof of the truth of the Bible and of the deity of Christ. Without seeing and beforehand, Jesus knew where the colt was and what would be done and said. Superhuman knowledge and mastery over nature are honors belonging to God. These are signs of deity.
Not All Joy

Matthew 21:10-11 And when he was come into Jerusalem, all the city was moved–Josephus estimates two and one-half million to have attended the Passover. A great multitude, indeed, witnessed this great event in history.

In the midst of the joy was grief. Jesus was grieving that although He came to save all, not all would be saved. Luke tells us that Jesus beheld the city, and wept over it, Saying, If thou hadst known . . . the things which belong unto thy peace! There, laid out before Him was a city, beyond it a nation, and beyond that a world so blinded by sin as to refuse the thing it needed most. This, not His own coming suffering and death, brought tears from the heart of Jesus.

God was ready to give to the world what the people had waited for and longed for during centuries, namely, the Messiah and His kingdom. But these foolish ones only looked around and in cold indifference, as the Messiah came into the city, asked, "Who is this?" No doubt, many of these ones who cried Hosanna to the son of David at this hour, would cry, Crucify him in just a few days. Jesus is the King of the universe. Dear one, is He your King? And the multitude said, This is Jesus the prophet of Nazareth of Galilee. Here was their King, the Son of God, and when they were asked, they did not have the correct answer to give. They thought He was a mere prophet. A greater than a prophet was here, but these people, even after He had done such great works, did not recognize Him as Who He really was. What would your answer be?
JUST A THOUGHT
We cannot all play the same instrument, but we can all be in the same key.

JESUS NEARING HIS DEATH
Scripture Text: Mark 14:10-11, 18-21, 27-43

Jesus foresaw His death and knew it would be hard for the disciples to understand. Though it was a time of great distress for Him, He did not forget to show them the real meaning of His suffering. Judas was chosen by Jesus to be one of the twelve disciples. He was in the very presence of Jesus, physically, yet he separated from Him spiritually. Why? What happened in between that made him seek a way to betray Jesus to His enemies? Did he fail to watch and pray? Did he allow evil thoughts and desires to come and remain in his heart? Let us see what God's eternal Word has to say about the answers to these questions. Compare with Matthew 26:36-46.
MEMORY VERSE: . . . O my Father, if it be possible, let this cup pass from me: nevertheless not as I will, but as thou wilt. Matthew 26:39
The Sinful Plot

Mark 14:10-11 And Judas Iscariot, one of the twelve . . . Judas was chosen by Jesus to preach the Gospel. He was given power over unclean spirits and to heal disease. Went unto the chief priests to betray Him unto them. The priests wanted revenge. They allowed a spirit of resentment to work in their hearts and cause them to murder Jesus. Judas failed to watch and pray, as many do today, and allowed the spirit of greed to place the love of money before his love for Jesus. Both being evil, they bargained together to do evil. When we have a spirit that desires to betray Jesus, the enemy will make it convenient to do so.

Mark 14:18-21 One of you . . . shall betray me. This was a most serious moment in the life of Judas. He was about to be turned over to Satan, but Jesus, by naming him out, offered him one last opportunity to repent. Judas failed in his time of visitation. How about you, dear one? Judas had to suffer the consequences of his decision. So will each of us. Judas went out and it was night (John 13:30). When one turns from Jesus, He always goes into darkness.
It Is Possible to Fall

Mark 14:27-31 Walking from Jerusalem to Gethsemane, Jesus said, All ye shall be offended–all the disciples would be turned aside from Him. A lack of spiritual power and weakness in the flesh would cause this. Fear and bewildered disappointment would cause all of the disciples to be offended because of Jesus. Peter would even deny Him. Jesus quoted the prophecy which He was fulfilling (Zechariah 13:7). But he spake . . . I will not deny thee . . . Likewise also said they all. Each man thought he was strong in himself. Jesus tried to help them to see and understand their weakness in themselves (1 Corinthians 10:11-12; 1 Peter 5:8-9).
Gethsemane

Mark 14:32-36 And they came to . . . Gethsemane . . . Sit ye here, while I shall pray. In Gethsemane Jesus left eight disciples waiting and went farther on with Peter, James, and John. Then He left them to wait and watch and went yet farther on to pray. Jesus needed their friendship. A terrific battle was raging in His heart, right against

wrong, God against Satan, the flesh against the spirit. His human nature and His divine nature were in a life-and-death struggle on which depended the salvation of lost mankind. The eternal fate of all the world was held in Jesus' hands. In this greatest battle and greatest victory that the world has ever known, all the powers of Satan and hell were hurled at Jesus. He was sore amazed–as the terrible ordeal loomed before Him, His human nature felt fear and great amazement.

The thing coming to pass was greater than He had expected. My soul is exceeding sorrowful unto death . . . If possible take away this cup. The terror He faced here was not a concern with the probability of physical pain. It was not of the body nor of the mind, but of the soul. Nevertheless not what I will, but what thou wilt. By keeping His trust in His Father, by submitting fully to Him, by deciding to carry out the plan they together had made, this great victory was won. It was the will of the Heavenly Father that Jesus suffer and die. There in prayer, alone, Jesus won the victory for all time. On Calvary He only carried it out. Jesus received no as an answer to His prayer that if it were possible this cup would be taken away. No is sometimes God's will. To seek and accept God's will is real prayer.
The Flesh Is Weak

Mark 14:37-43 And he cometh, and findeth them sleeping . . . couldest not thou watch one hour? What a small favor to ask one who had made such broad statements earlier. Lip service only. How much might the disciples have learned if they had stayed awake, watched, and prayed with Jesus! Watch ye and pray, lest ye enter into temptation–this is the only way through which temptation loses its power. When Jesus said to Peter, the flesh is weak, He could speak from His own present experience with that flesh. Because He knows and conquered it, He is able to make us conquerors also (Hebrews 2:18).

The problem of suffering is one of the most difficult with which Christianity has to deal. The suffering of the saints and of those who live holy, blameless lives remains as a bewildering issue to the human race. Atheism and unbelievers have never come up with any satisfactory answer. Christianity faces the problem firmly because of the fact that Jesus Himself suffered. It is a part of God's will and plan that His followers suffer for His cause (1 Peter 2:21; 4:1; 2 Timothy 2:12). We must heed His warning through God's Word. Jesus knows all the ways that we are weak. He will give us strength to endure to the end. As we try to flee from trouble because it is painful, we miss the spiritual structure it is designed to work in us.
JUST A THOUGHT
People seem to be able to stand adversity but not prosperity.

JESUS BEFORE THE HIGH PRIEST
Scripture Text: Mark 14:43-72

It is good to compare this Scripture reading with Matthew 26:47-75. Jesus and eleven of the disciples were in the Garden of Gethsemane. Jesus had prayed, gained the victory over His fleshly nature, and made the final decision to suffer for the sins of the world. The high priest asked Jesus, Art thou the Christ, the Son of the Blessed? In Matthew 22:42 Jesus asked, What think ye of Christ, whose son is he? If His Father was God, then Christ is God. This is the vital point in all of His work and teaching. This is where He received His authority and power to do what He claimed. The charge against Jesus was false. This is still a vital point to each of us. Read Isaiah, Chapter 53.

JESUS TRIED AND CRUCIFIED
Scripture Text: Mark 15:1-39

In this lesson today we once again relate to the happening in history that is so great it is beyond our comprehension, and yet so simple that even children may understand when told how great God's love is for all mankind.

The few hours between Christ's victory in Gethsemane and this lesson's events held the trial of Jesus, the denial of Peter, the release of Barabbas, and the cruel actions by the soldiers. Jesus' acceptance of it all showed more strength than to have fought back. No fault was found in Jesus. It was sin that crucified Him, your sin and mine. Jesus took our place. It takes love to die for good people, but greater love to die for sinners and enemies. All three courts where Jesus appeared allowed their Prisoner to be abused contrary to their laws. What faces a land whose courts become corrupted?
MEMORY VERSE: But God commendeth his love toward us, in that, while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us. Romans 5:8
Jesus Condemned

Mark 15:1-21 In the morning . . . bound Jesus . . . delivered him to Pilate, the Roman governor. It had been night when Caiaphas and his court tried Jesus and condemned Him to death. Therefore, in the morning, the group went to Pilate, accused Jesus, and asked for His death. Jesus gave no answer, even though Jewish law had no authority to put Him to death. Pilate marvelled that Jesus answered nothing. Because Jesus was a Galilean, Pilate sent Him to King Herod who found no reason to condemn Him and, after mocking Him, sent Him back (Luke 23:6-11). Pilate found no fault in Jesus and desired to release Him. His human thinking led him to believe that the people would rather have Jesus released than Barabbas. How wrong he was! Release Barabbas . . . Crucify . . . the King of the Jews. The people, led by the chief religious persons of the land, clamored for Jesus to die. They chose Barabbas instead of Jesus to be released at the Passover time. Is the world much different in their choice in our day? Pilate yielded, scourged Jesus, and gave Him to be crucified. Pilate was deceived in his heart to believe that a pan of water could wash away the guilt of his action (Matthew 27:24).

The soldiers considered the Prisoner fair prey for their degenerate "fun." They used a purple robe, crown of thorns, and a reed to ridicule His claim to being King. They saluted and bowed in fun. They insulted, spit upon, and struck Him. Through it all, Jesus made no resistance. Then they led him out to crucify him.
Jesus Crucified

Mark 15:22-32 They bring him unto . . . Golgotha. Now sin had its full way. They gave him to drink wine mingled with myrrh. It would be of no help, so He refused it. Crucified him–they nailed him to the Cross. Parted his garments–the soldiers divided His clothes (Psalm 22:18). Crucifixion meant the worst of human savagery inflicting the most intense human suffering. THE KING OF THE JEWS–did Pilate believe it true? (See John

18:33-39; 19:19-22.) With him they crucify two thieves–treated as one of them. The Scripture in Isaiah 53:12 was fulfilled. Railed on him, wagging their heads . . . They used sarcastic, taunting remarks emphasized by gestures. Ah, thou that destroyest the temple . . . Jesus had not said the temple but this temple, meaning His body (John 2:18-21). Save thyself–they spoke three days too soon. Jesus was taking their place, but they did not know it. Why did He take it? He did not have to. He did it to save those who did not deserve it but needed it. It is of no use unless we believe and accept Him. Sin, yours and mine and all mankind's, brought Jesus to the Cross. These people did not know that what they asked was the destruction of their only chance of salvation. The shame of the Cross does not lay on Christ but on the men who nailed Him there. Chief priests mocking said . . . He saved others; himself he cannot save. They little knew the truth they spoke. He knew He could not save both and had sealed His choice the night before. Let Christ . . . descend . . . that we may see and believe. Belief does not come from seeing but by believing.
The Death of Jesus

Mark 15:33-39 Sixth hour . . . darkness . . . until the ninth hour. This assault of evil against righteousness, against God, was of such tragic proportion that God darkened the sun for three hours. Spiritual darkness reigned temporarily. One of the dying thieves reviled Jesus. But one, repenting, was the first to receive the salvation Jesus was dying to provide. My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me? The sins of the whole world that Jesus bore separated Him from His Father. That is the nature of sin (Isaiah 59:2). Perhaps this was the lowest point in Jesus' whole life. Satan and hell were doing their worst. Jesus was doing His best. Jesus cried with a loud voice. In John 19:30 Jesus said, It is finished. The whole plan of salvation was finished. Here was a cry of victory, a shout of triumph. Thank God! He commended His spirit to His Father, and gave up the ghost–died.

At the same time the veil of the temple was rent in twain. This was the curtain which divided the holy place from the holiest place. As the veil opened the way into the holiest place of the temple, so Christ's death opened the way to God (Hebrews 10:19-20). A hand from Heaven did it. Those looking on knew these were no ordinary events. No longer was man held off from God with a priest representing him once a year. Now each saint is a priest, free to come all the way to God through the Holy Spirit's indwelling. If you do not have this experience, it is waiting for you. To the Christian, death is not a dead-end street; it is a triumphal door through which he may pass on to the joys of an eternal home. Truly this man was the Son of God–the centurion believed.
JUST A THOUGHT
Human nature has not improved so very much since the day of the Cross. Shameful motives still cause men to crucify our Lord afresh daily.

JESUS' RESURRECTION
Scripture Texts: Matthew 28:1-10; 1 Corinthians 15:20-21

Christ's Resurrection is the completion of the plan that He came to establish by dying. Without the Resurrection all would have been ended and lost. It is the greatest of all miracles. The Resurrection stands joined with the Crucifixion at the highest point of history. The day following the Crucifixion was of the darkest the world has ever known.

It is a blow to any group to have their leader taken from them by death. But with the message of the Resurrection, the brokenhearted jumped up and faced a new day with glad hearts. Christ crucified and risen again was the main burden of the Apostles' preaching. Jesus never spoke of His approaching Crucifixion without speaking, also, of His Resurrection.
MEMORY VERSE: Yet a little while, and the world seeth me no more; but ye see me: because I live, ye shall live also. John 14:19
Faithfulness Paid Off

When Jesus died, Joseph of Arimathaea and Nicodemus buried Jesus in Joseph's new tomb as believing women stood nearby. Pilate, sick and tired of the whole affair, wearily consented to the sealing of the tomb.

Matthew 28:1-4 In the end of the sabbath, as it began to dawn toward the first day of the week–before daybreak on Sunday. The women brought spices and ointments for the body of Jesus. Great earthquake–earth and Heaven alike were being shaken. A great turning point in history had arrived. Nature sounded out the event even as when Jesus died. The cause of this earthquake is told–for the angel of the Lord descended. Here was God Himself, His angels, and His people working in unity and harmony in His plan for all of His kingdom together. Rolled back the stone–man had sealed it. Sat upon it–symbolic of Heaven's contempt for man's power and estimate of events. Man's rules cannot hinder God's plan. His countenance was like lightning, and his raiment white as snow–reminding of Jesus' transfiguration. Keepers did shake–those guarding against the stealing of Jesus' body were frightened. Fear is one of mankind's greatest enemies. Faith is the only cure for fear. Not faith in ourselves, not faith in anything the world can offer, but faith in Jesus, who had been crucified, but now was raised from the dead and glorified. The removing of the stone had nothing to do with Christ's coming out of the tomb. It was only so the people could see the empty tomb.

Matthew 28:5-7 Angel . . . said . . . Fear not ye . . . He is not here–He did not belong here among the dead. He is life; He could not stay. The dark, dead tomb could not hold life and light, Jesus Christ. Thank God! He is now Savior of all the world. All the power of Satan could not hold Him there. He is risen, as he said–told them plainly, recalled Jesus' own words. Now they understood what before they did not. Come, see the place–no concealment. God wanted them to have proof. Truth can afford to lay bare the facts. The angels (Luke 24:4 tells of two) stayed to send the women with word to the disciples. Go quickly, and tell . . . he is risen from the dead . . . he goeth before you into Galilee. God wanted the facts of the Resurrection known. The command was GO and TELL. This is still the command to Christian believers concerning the good news of a living Christ. Christianity is a missionary religion. They were to meet Him at some point in Galilee. We have definite appointments with Him–our daily

devotions, the carrying of His righteousness in our everyday lives to others, attendance to church services of worship, and a faithful performance of the tasks He give us to do. He goes before us in all these things. When we keep these appointments, we see Him, not with the eyes of the flesh, but with spiritual discernment.
Jesus Met Them

Matthew 28:8-10 They–the women–departed quickly . . . with fear and great joy. In the early dawn, picture the women running to bring his disciples word of news never carried before. How their hearts beat and leaped for great joy. How can some teach that women have no part in the church? Here women carried the first God-sent message of Christ's resurrection. This was the beginning of a new position in the world for womanhood. Up to that time, even among the spiritual-minded, a woman was an inferior creature, the servant of a man. Yet it was to women that Jesus first appeared. From that time until the present, women have held a place of honor in the Church of God. Jesus met them, saying, All hail. Joy so overwhelmed them that they only worshipped him, falling down before Him, for they held him by the feet–the first service of divine worship of the risen Christ. Then said Jesus . . . Be not afraid–the familiar Jesus, tenderly driving away fear. Go tell my brethren–those weak, confused, doubting men who had forsaken Him when He needed them most, even denied Him. He in His moment of greatest triumph, called them my brethren. That they go into Galilee, and there shall they see me. What great anticipation this must have stirred within the hearts of these brethren! They did see Him there.
Christ, the Firstfruits

First Corinthians 15:20 Now is Christ risen–it is sure–and become the firstfruits–He was the first to have a glorified body. We will have such bodies at the coming Resurrection Day when all are raised from death.

Jesus actually arose in body. If not, He did not arise at all. Jesus' resurrection is the guarantee of ours. He said, Because I live, ye shall live also (John 14:19). When we arise, we will have bodies. Jesus did, and we shall be like him (1 John 3:2). Our bodies will be fashioned like unto his glorious body (Philippians 3:21). The saints can look to 1 Corinthians, Chapter 15 and find the following: Sown in corruption; raised in incorruption: Sown in dishonor; raised in glory: Sown in weakness; raised in power: Sown a natural body; raised a spiritual body: Sown in the image of the earthly; raised in the image of the Heavenly. Sown a mortal; raised an immortal: Sown in death; raised in victory. The Resurrection makes the difference.
JUST A THOUGHT
Many things are worse than defeat, and compromise with evil is one of them.

blocks.text: Sunday School Material for Adults 1
L ESSO N 8
JESUS APPEARS AFTER RESURRECTION
Scripture Texts: John 20:19,20, 24-29; John 21:1-14

Following His Resurrection Jesus was not with His disciples constantly as before. His body seemed freed from the limitations of space and matter in ways not described. He appeared and vanished suddenly, passing through closed doors. Yet He was the same loving Jesus as always. The main portion of His work was completed when He arose. He remained forty days to give proof of His Resurrection, to comfort and settle His disciples after the shattering experience of the Crucifixion, and to give final teaching and instructions for the spread of the Gospel. Very important to us are these instructions, for they rest on our lives to carry out. The close of each Gospel Book records them.
The disciples had abundant proof of the Resurrection of Jesus in the many appearances of Him to them. We study some today.
MEMORY VERSE: And they said one to another, Did not our heart burn within us, while he talked with us by the way, and while he opened to us the scriptures? Luke 24:32
Evening After Resurrection

John 20:19-20 The same day at evening–the day He arose. Luke 24:13-32 tells us of Jesus meeting two disciples earlier in the day on the road to Emmaus. The doors were shut where the disciples were assembled for fear of the Jews–fear that the recent violence to Jesus might fall on them. They were a marked people. Is not it yet so in our day? Came Jesus–the shut doors did not hinder Him. Peace be unto you–the same loving Jesus bringing peace to troubled hearts. They needed His peace, and we need it too. (Luke 24:33-40 tells of the same appearing.) Shewed . . . his hands and his side–His wounds proved that it was Jesus. Also, that He had come through death with the same body.
John 20:24-25 Thomas . . . said . . . Except I shall see . . . and put . . . and thrust . . . I will not believe--Thomas had to be shown.
One Week Later

John 20:26-29 After eight days–a little more than a week later. Again Jesus came through shut doors and appeared with the same greeting as before. Thomas was with them this time. Saith he to Thomas, Reach hither thy finger–He knew Thomas' unbelief and what he had said. He gave the proof he asked. Be not faithless, but believing. He was not pleased with Thomas' doubt. The sin of unbelief locks out all of God's graces. All His stay here Jesus had to urge people to believe. Now at its close, He still has to. We are prone, like Thomas, to doubt unless we see, and sometimes after we see. This grieves God. Faith is that arm by which we reach and take hold of God and His blessings. We must have faith. Jesus sets no limits to the possibilities of faith. Why should we? He said, ". . . all things are possible to him that believeth" (Mark 9:23).

Thomas answered . . . My Lord and my God. Immediately his faith took hold in Jesus, and he knew Him as God. Because thou hast seen me, thou hast believed–this is better than a stubborn spirit of unbelief which will not believe even though it sees. But better yet, is the childlike faith that believes without seeing. Jesus called such blessed.

Sunday School Material for Adults 2
At the Seashore

John 21:1-11 At the sea of Tiberias–same as Galilee. The disciples had gone to Galilee as He had said (Matthew 28:10). Seven are together. Peter saith unto them, I go a fishing–confused and uncertain, he turned to his old life. Caught nothing–the old life is never the same when turning back to it after living with Jesus. God planned it that way. Jesus stood on the shore: but the disciples knew not that it was Jesus. Whether their eyes were holden (as in Luke 24:16), or His appearance was changed, we do not know. Jesus saith . . . Children, have ye any meat–have you caught any fish? They answered him, No–a simple, honest answer. Jesus now prepared them for their last catch. From now on, they would turn to a different occupation in life, that of fishing for men. Cast the net on the right side–Jesus knows where the catch can be made, if it be fish or men. And they caught a multitude of fishes. (Compare Luke 5:4-8.) Perhaps the miracle reminded John. At least, he knew Jesus then. Fire of coals there, and fish . . . and bread. Jesus was still providing for their needs. Once He had blessed another's bread and fish to feed the people. This day He provided His own bread and meat. Jesus is still providing bread and meat for the souls of all men who are poor in spirit. There were so many, yet was not the net broken–another miracle.
Jesus' Invitation

John 21:12-14 Come and dine–inviting them to eat with Him. Taketh bread, and giveth them, and fish likewise. The Master, victorious over all things, still desiring to serve others. None . . . durst ask . . . knowing . . . it was the Lord. They knew, yet there seems a strangeness, an awe of Him. No doubt, condemnation for their earlier failures caused them to be estranged. Failure to do right always brings a strangeness to our relationship with Jesus. Third time that Jesus shewed himself–that is, to a group of the eleven. Ten definite appearances are mentioned, whether they were all, we do not know. Has Jesus appeared to you? What is your response?
JUST A THOUGHT
Anything which separates children of God is foreign to God's plan.

L ESSO N 9
JESUS' ASCENSION
Scripture Texts: Acts 1:1-12; John 14:3

Jesus showed Himself alive after His passion by many proofs. To the Jews, Jesus is a martyr who died for a great cause two thousand years ago. But He is set forth in the New Testament as more than a martyr. God raised Him from the dead, and He is a glorified and risen Savior. He returned from the grave to be with His disciples for a period of forty days, appearing to them time and again during this time.

Jesus' leaving of the world was as unique as the rest of His life. It was a miracle. His death was not the end. The Resurrection was not all. His ascension out of the world was not the end. Every step but leads on to the next one. Today we look at what the Scripture tells of His ascension.
MEMORY VERSE: And if I go and prepare a place for you, I will come again, and receive you unto myself; that where I am, there ye may be also. John 14:3
Seen Forty Days

Acts 1:1-3 The former treatise–a written composition on a particular subject. The same writer wrote the Book of Luke for the same friend, Theophilus. In the Book of Luke he had given Christ's doings and teachings until His Ascension–the day in which he was taken up. In Acts he tells of the Ascension more fully and goes on with the history of the church immediately following. After that he (Jesus) through the Holy Ghost had given commandments–He and the Holy Ghost worked together, as well as with the Father. To whom–to the Apostles–he shewed himself alive . . . by many infallible proofs . . . forty days–we have studied some of these proofs.
Stay at Jerusalem

Acts 1:4-5 Assembled together . . . commanded . . . not depart from Jerusalem–without His command they probably would have returned to Galilee. The Resurrection had changed the mood of the disciples from despair to joy. But there was uncertainty as to what they were expected to do, and they were reluctant to take the first step, whatever it might be. Jesus settled this by charging them not to depart from Jerusalem, but wait for the promise of the Father. What promise? Read Luke 24:49–Ye be endued with power from on high–a promise of power from God for the great work ahead of them. John truly baptized with water; but ye shall be baptized with the Holy Ghost . . . This promise was about to be fulfilled.

Acts 1:6-8 They asked . . . wilt thou at this time restore . . . the kingdom . . . ? Israel was under the foreign rule of Rome. The disciples had a mistaken idea that Jesus' mission was to win independence for Israel. It is not for you to know . . . They did not understand, as yet, the real nature of Christ's kingdom. Holy Spirit baptism would give them understanding. But ye shall receive power–not political power but spiritual–after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you: and ye shall be witnesses–He turned their eyes toward their true life's work. L ESSO N 10
JESUS APPEARS TO STEPHEN
Scripture Texts: Acts 6:8-15; Acts 7:51-60

Stephen's vision of Jesus was evidence that Jesus still lived as much as ever, and that He went to Heaven from the earth. The church knew this by faith in His Word, by the works He continued to do through them, and by the Presence of the Holy Spirit Whom He had promised to send. This sight of Him, as studied in today's lesson, was added evidence to them and to us. The whole history of the church is one long proof that Jesus lives. A few times, He gave added proof in a visible appearance. We study one today, that of His appearance to Stephen, the first person in the Church of God to wear the crown of martyrdom. Witnessing to the truth has in all ages raised opposition. Stephen summoned his generation to new spiritual heights.
MEMORY VERSE: And said, Behold, I see the heavens opened, and the Son of man standing on the right hand of God. Acts 7:56
A Faithful New Witness

We read in Acts 6:1 that when the number of the disciples was multiplied, there arose a murmuring . . . Murmuring concerning others' success always leads to trouble. Certain of the Greek-speaking Jews believed that their widows were being neglected in the distribution of food and other necessities in favor of the widows of other Jews. The Apostles brought the matter before the whole church and asked them to seek out seven men who were full of the Holy Ghost and wisdom, and put them in charge of this affair.

Acts 6:8-11 And Stephen–a Greek-speaking Jew, one of the seven chosen for this special work of distributing food to the needy, made this an opportunity to do a great spiritual service. The name Stephen means "crown." Full of faith and power, did great wonders and miracles--a true and active saint. He had power because the Holy Ghost had come upon him (verse 5). Then there arose Greek-speaking Jews–disputing with Stephen. They still were not satisfied. This kind of spirit in people cannot be satisfied by attempting to appease it. Active, successful work for the Lord always brings opposition. And they were not able to resist the wisdom and the spirit by which he spake. When his opponents were not able to withstand his wisdom, their thoughts turned to violence. Suborned men–procured privately or unlawfully and bribed them to twist the words of Stephen. They claimed that they had heard him speak blasphemous words against Moses, and against God, which indicates that these men put Moses and God on the same level. This was true blasphemy.
Stephen Before the Council

Acts 6:12-15 They stirred up the people . . . caught him, and brought him to the council–to the Sanhedrin. False witnesses–they twisted what had been said about the temple and the Law, Jesus' words about the temple of His body (John 2:19-21), and the relation of the Gospel to the Law. Only the Holy Spirit can reveal these things, and they did not understand them. Saw his face as . . . the face of an angel–the Holy Spirit showing in his face. When the high priest asked if these things were so, Stephen took the opportunity to preach a sermon by recounting the history of Israel to show (1) that the favor and worship of God are not confined to places, as the temple, and (2)

Sunday School Material for Adults 2
that Israel had always wandered from God and rebelled against Him.
The Council Before Stephen

Acts 7:51-54 Stephen ended his sermon with a direct accusation–Ye stiffnecked and uncircumcised–stubborn and unpurified–ye do always resist the Holy Ghost: as your fathers did–as he had just told them earlier. Prophets . . . persecuted? and they have slain them which shewed . . . coming of the Just One–who foretold of Jesus' coming–of whom ye . . . betrayers and murderers. Stephen boldly accused them of Christ's Crucifixion, which was true, and also of the murder of those who had spoken the Law of God down through their history. Received the law by . . . angels–angels had brought the message direct from God–and have not kept it–yet they tried to limit Stephen to it. Christianity was not to be a mere secondary associate of Judaism–it was to go forth and conquer the world, and Stephen recognized this early. His words struck a tender spot. They were cut to the heart. Greatly angered they gnashed . . . with their teeth–stooped to behavior of enraged animals. When they heard unpleasant truths spoken about themselves, the religious council turned into a furious mob.
Jesus Appears to Stephen

Acts 7:55-56 Stephen, full of the Holy Ghost, looked up stedfastly–intently looked to God–saw the glory of God, and Jesus standing . . . said . . . I see the heavens opened . . . Son of man standing on the right hand of God. Stephen's eyes were turned to Jesus, and the eyes of Jesus were turned to Stephen. His hands were held out to welcome Stephen to his eternal reward. This is symbolic of the eternal Christ who is standing at this very moment, offering His support and power to every one of us as we struggle against evil and adversity. Cried out . . . and stopped their ears–as millions through the ages have done when the truth becomes unpleasant to their hearts. Since they had no arguments to withstand him, they would drown him out with noise. And ran upon him–a wild mob–cast him out of the city–killings were done outside the city–and stoned him.
Stephen's Spirit

Acts 7:57-60 Witnesses–witnesses were to cast the first stones. They laid down their clothes–removed their outer coats at . . . feet of Saul. (See Acts 22:20.) We will hear more of Saul in a lesson to come. They stoned Stephen, calling upon God–his faith still firm in God–saying, Lord Jesus, receive my spirit–reminding us of Jesus' dying Words. Lord, lay not this sin to their charge--also reminds us of Jesus' prayer for His murderers. Stephen had no bitterness or desire for revenge, only love and forgiveness. He fell asleep–he died. In Acts 8:2 we learn that devout men buried Stephen with great lamentation. Men like Stephen are greatly loved (as well as greatly hated), greatly missed, and greatly welcomed in Heaven.

Let us consider the similarity of Stephen's death with that of Jesus. Stephen was condemned by the council as was Jesus. The mob cried out against Stephen as it had some time earlier against Jesus. They dragged Stephen out of the city to stone him, just as they dragged Jesus out of the city to crucify Him. Stephen died praying for his enemies; the Words on the lips of Jesus were for the forgiveness of His murderers.
Stephen had a brief career. He preached but one sermon. But his soul burned as a fiery furnace for the cause of his Lord. Are you willing to suffer for your devotion to the Lord Jesus?

L ESSO N 11
JESUS APPEARS TO PAUL
Scripture Text: Acts 9:1-20

Compare our Scripture text with Acts 22:1-16. Similar to Stephen in fearlessness, zeal, and sincerity was the young man whose name was Saul. But he was on the other side. When Stephen was stoned to death, Saul was consenting to it. After that, he made havoc of the church, entering into every house, and haling men and women, committed them to prison, and killed some. He was a Jew of the tribe of Benjamin and was a Pharisee (Philippians 3:5). He was born a Roman citizen in Tarsus (Acts 22:27-28). He studied in Jerusalem under Gamaliel, a leading teacher of the Law. He may have been one of them of Cilicia who disputed with Stephen.
MEMORY VERSE: I was not disobedient unto the heavenly vision. Acts 26:19
Saul's Character and Zeal

Acts 9:1-2 Saul, yet breathing out threatenings and slaughter against the disciples of the Lord–so full of hatred toward followers of Jesus that it came out in words, actions, and attitude. Saul's persecutions had mostly been confined to the city of Jerusalem. The murder of Stephen had caused the enemies of the Jerusalem church to step up persecutions so severe that the saints had scattered, seeking safety. Probably nothing else could have spread the Gospel so fast. They went every where preaching the word (Acts 8:4). Now he went unto the high priest, and desired . . . letters–permits–if he found any of this way–Christ's way–might bring them bound–take them prisoners. Now he had proper authority to go beyond the bounds of Jerusalem–to Damascus to the synagogues–a Syrian city located 150 miles away. This indicated the unmercifulness of Saul's zeal.
Saul's Vision of Jesus

Acts 9:3-9 Suddenly there shined round about him–it came suddenly–a light from heaven–over him from above. It was about noon, and the light was above the brightness of the sun. No doubt, this was the same light which had shown on the face of Moses and later was seen in the transfiguration. It blinded Saul. Fell to the earth–powerless–a voice . . . Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me? Jesus and His people are so closely united that harm to them strikes Him. Saul thought he was persecuting Jesus' followers only. When people persecute Christians, they persecute Christ. Who art thou, Lord?–knew it was One greater than himself. I am Jesus–he saw Jesus and heard Him speak to him (Acts 9:27), and in 1 Corinthians 9:1, he declares to have seen Jesus. What a revelation to Saul! He had thought Jesus an imposter, a mere man claiming to be the Messiah, attempting to overthrow the Jewish religion. I verily thought with myself, that I ought to do many things contrary to the name of Jesus (Acts 26:9). Hard for thee to kick against the pricks–as an ox kicking back against the goad would but injure itself. Saul was beginning to be pricked in conscience, and he was opposing the stirring of conscience and reason which God had set moving in his heart by Stephen's example and the spirit in which other saints had met Saul's persecutions. There was conflict in Saul's mind. He was not at peace, even with the papers of authority. The long journey to Damascus had given him time to think over his actions, and he was in a good state of mind to receive the vision and the call.

Trembling and astonished–greatly affected by fear and astonishment–Lord, what wilt thou have me to do?–complete surrender, no conditions. This was the turning point in Saul's life. It was here that he turned from

doing what he thought he ought to do, and did what the Lord wanted him to do. From persecuting Jesus, he turns to serving Him. Arise, and go into the city, and it shall be told thee–instead of Jesus telling him Himself, He had a man there to do it. He reserved that work for one of His followers. He uses men and women to do this work, making it an opportunity for both the giver and receiver to have a blessing. The men . . . with him . . . speechless, hearing a voice . . . seeing no man–they heard the voice but did not understand the Words. Saul only, saw Jesus and understood the Words. (Read Acts 26:13-15.) Saul arose . . . saw no man–blind–led him by the hand . . . The one who led others, bound, to prison, is now being led to Damascus.
The Street Called Straight

Acts 9:10-16 And the Lord said . . . go into the street . . . called Straight, and enquire in the house of Judas for . . . Saul. Ananias was in shape spiritually for the Lord to use him. The directions are given in detail. Nothing is left to chance. Ananias knew exactly what he was supposed to do. For, behold, he prayeth. Saul, being a Pharisee, had said many prayers; now he was praying. He was praying in the right spirit and for the right cause. God was preparing Saul to receive Ananias and preparing Ananias to go to Saul. When God sends us, He prepares the way before us. Ananias knew all about Saul, how he had persecuted the Christians even unto death. Nothing short of a vision from God would have motivated Ananias to go and call upon Saul. The Lord said unto him, Go . . . he is a chosen vessel unto me. God chooses the best. To bear my name before the Gentiles . . . Saul was to be an apostle first to the Gentiles. He stood before Gentile kings, and many Jews were saved under his ministry also.
Saul Received Sight

Acts 9:17-20 Ananias went–he believed and obeyed. Putting his hands on him, said, Brother Saul–Blessed title! He was a brother now, born into the family of God. Jesus . . . hath sent me, that thou mightest receive thy sight–physical sight–and be filled with the Holy Ghost–spiritual sight, the Holy Spirit would lead and direct him from now on. Immediately . . . fell . . . scales . . . he received sight . . . arose . . . baptized–no hesitation. Saved people want to obey. Straightway he preached Christ . . . that he is the Son of God. Saul had just learned this, and he could not keep it still. It was burning in his soul.
When Was Saul Saved?

Who can know for certain when Saul was saved? Salvation is a change from a condition of danger to one of safety, a transfer from the power of darkness to the kingdom of his dear Son, from serving Satan to serving God, from death in sin to life in Christ. Between the time Saul fell to the earth and when he arose from the earth a mighty change took place. He fell in rebellion against Jesus; he rose submitted to Him. He fell an unbeliever; he rose a believer. He fell a persecutor; he rose to pray. Saul received his sight. Have you received yours?
JUST A THOUGHT
A church membership does not make one a Christian any more than owning a piano makes one a musician.

JESUS APPEARS TO JOHN
Scripture Text: Revelation 1:9-18

The Apostle John, toward the end of his distinguished ministry, suffered persecution at the hands of the Roman emperor, Domitian, about A.D. 95. He had long been pastor of the church in Ephesus and the man of God to whom the churches in Asia looked as their leader. It was to be expected that a man of his standing, the last surviving Apostle of the original twelve, should have felt upon himself the heavy hand of Roman cruelty. He was sent to the Isle of Patmos, a small island in the Aegean Sea, a short distance from Ephesus. He speaks of himself as a brother and partaker with the other disciples in the tribulation and kingdom and patience which are in Jesus.
Evidences multiply of Christ's resurrection and His continued life in Heaven. Now we look at His appearance to John.
MEMORY VERSE: I am he that liveth, and was dead; and, behold, I am alive for evermore, Amen. Revelation 1:18
Our Brother and Companion

Revelation 1:9 I John–the Apostle–brother . . . companion in tribulation–he was just like us, human, suffered the same trials and limitations as we, also was persecuted. We may tend to feel that Bible characters were so far above us that God could do for them things He will not do for us. This is not true. They all had the same limitations and temptations, the same danger of falling as we. And we have the same promises, the same spiritual provisions, the same access to God as they. In the kingdom and patience of Jesus Christ–had the same place in Christ's kingdom, the same hope in Him that all Christians have.

Let us examine these three things. Tribulation means suffering of a variety which cleanses the soul and makes it better. The tribulum, from which this word is derived, was the flail that separated the wheat from the chaff. Suffering makes many people bitter; when rightly endured–especially when endured in Christian faith–it makes men better. The kingdom or the rule of God was something which John shared with his brethren. They had that joyful hold on living reality which enabled them to live in peace and confidence even amid heavy persecutions. The patience which is in Jesus is a thing which we need to have–patience with ourselves, patience with others, patience with God, and patience with what appears to us to be His strange providences (Luke 21:19). In the isle . . . Patmos–where he had been placed in exile–for the word of God . . . testimony of Jesus Christ–his banishment was persecution for his faith in and preaching of Christ and the Gospel. After the death of Domitian, John was returned to Ephesus.
John Hears Jesus

Revelation 1:10-11 In the Spirit–alone, banished, separated from the work and the people he loved, suffering hardship, still John had a place to go to reach Jesus. He retired into the chamber of his heart where the Holy Spirit lived. There he could worship, talk with the Lord, sup with Jesus on heavenly food, and feel the Spirit sweetly fill his heart to overflowing. If we have the Holy Spirit, we, like John, can be in the Spirit and

find fellowship, joy, strength, courage, and spiritual food, regardless of circumstances. On the Lord's day–first day of the week. John could not meet with the saints, so he worshiped where he was. Heard . . . a great voice–a voice spoke to John on that day, and it had in it the triumph of a trumpet blast. John was given divine assurance that the destiny of the Christian and the church is triumph. I am Alpha and Omega . . . first . . . last–eternal. This was Jesus talking. Write–the Book of Revelation–send it unto the seven churches–real places and real people.
John Saw Jesus

Revelation 1:12-16 I turned . . . saw seven golden candlesticks . . . are the seven churches (verse 20). One like unto the Son of man–even in His changed appearance, John recognized Jesus, the One he had known in the flesh. Head and . . . hairs . . . white as snow . . . eyes . . . as a flame of fire . . . feet . . . as if they burned in a furnace–purity, richness, strength, omniscience, light and glory. Voice . . . many waters–power and majesty. All the attributes of God. Here Jesus is dressed in attire to put heat on the church. In his right hand seven stars–the pastors–of the seven churches. Christ held and guarded them in His hand. Out of his mouth . . . a sharp twoedged sword–judgment, the word of God (Hebrews 4:12). Countenance . . . as the sun shineth in his strength. All about Him proclaimed Him King, the Almighty in power. (Compare Matthew 17:2.)
John's Response

Revelation 1:17 I fell at his feet as dead–all strength gone, overwhelmed, a mere man before the great God. Submission and worship were so complete that there was an emptying out of all of John's being. He laid his right hand upon me–the same hand which held the ministers of the churches. Fear not–the same Fear not He so often used. It is no wonder John was fearful! This was a large responsibility being put on him. I am the first and the last–trust Me, John. I am the beginning, the ending, and everything in between. I fill all time and am eternal.
Jesus Alive Forevermore

Revelation 1:18 I am he that liveth–He IS life (John 14:6). He has life in Himself (John 5:26)–and was dead–He is the One John saw die on the Cross. While Jesus speaks of His life in the present and future tense, He speaks of His death only in the past. He is no longer on the Cross or in the grave. The crucifix (Christ fixed on the Cross) has no place in Christianity. Behold, I am alive for evermore–He can never be sacrificed again (Romans 6:9). He was offered once for all (Hebrews 10:10-14). We have a living Savior who cannot die again. Amen–it is sure, certain, true. So be it–the seal of certainty. Have the keys of hell and of death–Jesus has power over these. He will finally cast them both into the lake of fire (Revelation 20:14). This can be no other than Jesus! Oh, the love, the mercy, the gentle compassion of Jesus!
JUST A THOUGHT
A church that has to be supported by tea parties, ice cream socials, and fried chicken dinners is as weak as the tea, as cold as the ice cream, and as dead as the chicken.

L ESSO N 13
JESUS IN THE FUTURE
Scripture Texts: Matthew 16:27; 24:27; 25:31-33; Revelation 1:7; 1 Thessalonians 4:14-18; Revelation 19:7

We have looked at Jesus coming from past eternity, living on earth a brief time to redeem men, and now back home in Heaven with His Father for future eternity. We cannot study the end of His life. There is no end or "last" of Jesus Christ. Praise God! He lives on forever. Jesus does not want His people to only look back upon Him in the past. He has told us what to expect in the future.

God's whole program is one. There is unity in everything He does. ALL the saints will be taken together. Enoch and Abraham will be there, Peter, Paul, all down to the last one saved. There is no language to describe the glorious scene, all gathered together to see Jesus.
MEMORY VERSE: Therefore let us not sleep as do others; but let us watch and be sober. 1 Thessalonians 5:6
Christ's Second Coming

Matthew 16:27 Son of man shall come–Jesus is coming again–in the glory of his Father–we can only get a glimpse of this glory at Christ's transfiguration and other biblical scenes–with his angels–the angels have a close interest and a part in our salvation, yet they never had the privilege of experiencing the joy that salvation brings. In this event, ALL people will have a very vital interest, for then–at the time of His coming–he shall reward every man–both good and bad–according to his works–the deeds of our lives determine our judgment.
Matthew 24:27 As the lightning–sudden, for all to see, not secret. This is the way the Second coming of the Son of man shall be.
The Judgment

Matthew 25:31-33 When the Son . . . shall come in his glory . . . then shall he sit upon the throne–the Judgment seat of Christ (Romans 14:10-13). The great Savior is now the Judge of all. Before him shall be gathered all nations–not one person absent–he shall separate . . . sheep from the goats–symbolic of but two kinds of people. What a sad time for the goats! Do all possible to see them saved before that awful day! The judgment awaiting each is told in verses 34 and 41. There is more to the end of life than to die; a stern judgment follows (Hebrews 9:27). Jesus was Savior while He was on earth. At this moment He is our Mediator before the throne of grace. On the last day He will be our Judge.
Who Are Included?

Revelation 1:7 Behold, he cometh with clouds–as foretold when He ascended (Acts 1:9-11). Every eye shall see him–it is useless to claim that He has or will come secretly or unknown to even one person. And they also which pierced him–both the wicked and the saints, dead and alive, will see Him. Thus, the resurrection of all must precede this. (Read John 5:28-29).

First Thessalonians 4:14 If we believe that Jesus died and rose–just as sure as His death and Resurrection. Even so–our resurrection hinges on His. Them also which sleep in Jesus will God bring with him–the spirits of

the dead saints to be reunited with their new bodies.

First Thessalonians 4:15-18 We say unto you by the word of the Lord–not Paul's idea but God's Word –We which are alive and remain–the saints living on earth at the time of Christ's coming–shall not prevent them which are asleep–the dead saints. The only ones being considered here are saints, dead and alive. He tells us that the live saints will not go ahead of the dead saints. Lord himself shall descend from heaven with a shout, with the voice . . . and with the trump–the Voice which will bring them from the graves, heralding the event, calling forth the dead (1 Corinthians 15:51-52). The dead in Christ shall rise first. Then we which are alive–saints living at that time–caught up together–all the saints in one great multitude–in the clouds–just as Jesus left, He will be coming. To meet the Lord in the air: and so shall we ever be with the Lord–go to Heaven to be with Jesus and His Father forever. Oh! Thank God! For all time and eternity. Comfort one another with these words–testify to it. We are not told much of Heaven, but just the thought of the hope of attaining it is a comfort in life's trials and troubles to those of us who are saved from sin.

Note in these verses that our Lord assures us of the inevitability of the Judgment. No one will escape it. Our whole lives will someday be laid before us by a Judge whose wisdom is perfect, Who has every fact, good and bad alike before Him, and whose verdict will be set in accordance with the standards of perfect justice. He will make no mistakes.
The Bridegroom Cometh

Revelation 19:7 Let us be glad and rejoice, and give honour to him–to the Lamb, Jesus Christ–for the marriage of the Lamb is come–Christ's wedding day. His wife hath made herself ready–the church, ready by having washed their robes, and made them white in the blood of the Lamb (Revelation 7:14). Jesus will take His bride to the Heavenly home which He has prepared for her. There they will be together for all eternity. Are you ready and waiting for the Bridegroom to come? He could come at any time (Matthew 25:13).

This lesson closes this series, but it can find no period to the life of Christ. He is the One which is, and which was, and which is to come. Praise God! He will come for His bride, judge the world, then continue on as the Ruler, the Temple, and the Light of Heaven. Beyond that, we know not. That remains yet to be seen. We know it will be all good and will continue without end.
JUST A THOUGHT
There is no middle ground between good and evil.

THE TRANSFIGURATION OF JESUS
Scripture Text: Luke 9:28-36
In our study of the life of Christ and His work here on earth, we are
looking at Him as existing in past eternity and in future eternity as well as the
brief time He spent on earth. We have seen Him creating the universe with
His Father and the Holy Spirit, appearing on earth before His birth here,
promised to be sent to earth, and becoming human and living among men.
Now we come to the third and last year of His ministry. His unchanging
separation from, and denunciation of, evil has brought the enmity and
rejection of the masses to whom He had shown the power of God. He also
won the devoted loyalty of a few. Compare Mark 9:2-9 and Matthew 17:1-
MEMORY VERSE: And there came a voice out of the cloud, saying, This
is my beloved Son: hear him.
Luke 9:35
Christ Transfigured
Luke 9:28-29 Jesus took Peter and John and James, and went up into a mountain to pray. He wanted them
alone for the sacred scene to follow. Nothing like this had the eyes of man ever seen. It was too sacred for most to
see; these three great men could not handle it. They went to sleep while Jesus prayed. And as He prayed, the
fashion of his countenance was altered, and his raiment was white and glistering–A brighter scene than earth
affords, strange indeed. Jesus was changed. The glory of God shone through His human body. The veil put on Him
for His earthly stay was removed and showed briefly His inner glory, His true nature, and gave a glimpse of what
God is really like. God was honoring Him. The manifestation of God was so strong that it overflowed into the
material of His clothing.
Two Men Brought Back
Luke 9:30-31 Equally as miraculous as the change in Jesus was the bringing back of Moses and Elias (Elijah)
from the other world. There talked with Him two men . . . Moses and Elias. Moses was the great leader through
whom God gave the Law to Israel. He represents the dispensation of the Law. He died in 1451 B.C. Elias, one of
the greatest of the Prophets, represents God's government by the Prophets (1 Kings, Chapters 17, 18, 19, and 21).
He was translated some 925 years before; yet here they were living and talking. They were examples of the
everlasting life Jesus talked about. Once begun, no life ever ends. They were talking with Jesus of his decease
which he should accomplish at Jerusalem.
The Law with its forms and sacrifices pointed forward to Christ (Galatians 3:24). All of its types were fulfilled
in Jesus. The Prophets also pointed forward to Christ. His coming and salvation fulfilled their predictions. They
talked of Christ's death because it was the finish of the work in whose beginning they had so vital a part. God
brought these representatives of the Law and the Prophets back to hear from Christ Himself the plan for the glorious
finish of the program so long awaited by them. This was the climax of the purpose for which He came to earth.

God Drives Away Confusion
Luke 9:32-33 But Peter and they . . . were heavy with sleep: and when they were awake, they saw . . . It
is marvelous what God can show us if He can only get us awake. Peter said . . . quick-speaking Peter, usually too
quick–good for us to be here. What great company they were in; Peter wanted to stay there. Let us make three
tabernacles, one for thee . . . Moses . . . Elias: not knowing what he said. A great idea, but a man's idea. This is
where confusion begins. Every time men's ideas get them to believe that great men are equal to Jesus, they want to
build tabernacles to them, and more confusion is added to the minds of the people.
Luke 9:34 While he thus spake–God stops this kind of business very quickly. This was connected with Heaven.
His appearance was such as no earthly power could produce. Citizens of Heaven came for the occasion and a voice
from Heaven took part in it. Matthew 17:6 tells us they fell on their face, and were sore afraid. No wonder they
were afraid! Peter's words had caused a cloud to be placed over the whole wonderful scene. Where once they could
see plainly now a cloud had blinded their sight.
Luke 9:35 Voice out of the cloud, saying, This is my beloved Son: hear him. The Law and the Prophets are
not our guides now. Only Jesus Christ is to be obeyed. He is the Head of all things. The Voice of God named Jesus
His Son as the One to be heard and obeyed. Hear him. In these two words is the solution for the division and
confusion in the religious world, for all false doctrines, and for all the evils and troubles of the world today.
See Jesus Only
Luke 9:36 Jesus was found alone. When the Voice of God was past, they saw no one else but Jesus. Jesus told
them to tell the vision to no man (Matthew 17:8-9). The vision was over. Jesus commanded secrecy concerning
this until after He was risen again from the dead. Jesus did not want them to tell about visions. He wanted them
to tell the Gospel. They did not understand and Jesus did not want them to speak that which they did not understand.
After His death they would be given understanding of all things by the Holy Spirit. His rising would be the greatest
proof of His Deity.
JUST A THOUGHT
"The only test of fellowship is the existence
of fellowship." – D.S. Warner

JESUS' RAISING OF LAZARUS
Scripture Text: John 11:1-44
Today we find Jesus in contact with the home of Lazarus, Mary, and
Martha. Lazarus is sick unto death, and the sisters send to Jesus an urgent
message. It was amazing to the sisters that Jesus made no immediate
response to their call in behalf of their brother. When Jesus finally arrived
at Bethany, Martha met Him with much sorrow. She said, "Lord if thou
hadst been here, my brother had not died." Jesus replied, "I am the
resurrection, and the life: he that believeth in me, though he were dead, yet shall he live." Jesus did not say that
resurrection came about through Him. He said, "I AM the resurrection, and the life."
MEMORY VERSE: Jesus said unto her, I am the resurrection, and the life: he that believeth in me, though he
were dead, yet shall he live.
John 11:25
Death of Lazarus
John 11:1-17 A certain man was sick . . . Lazarus . . . Mary and her sister Martha. This event occurred just
before Jesus entered Jerusalem for the last week before His crucifixion–a very busy week before He faced the Cross.
It seemed amazing to the sisters–as it would to us until we read the complete story through–that Jesus was in no
hurry to go to them. Here we see an example of those strange delays of the divine which so often bewilder us. But
within these delays are wrapped some of God's richest blessings. It is hard to see how such a misfortune can be for
the glory of God. It was not fear of the Jews that kept Him away, such as His disciples felt for Him (verse 8). Jesus'
actions were planned. He lived as continual Master of every situation. He saw the end from the beginning.
Lazarus is dead. How did Jesus know? No messenger had come to Him. I am glad . . . I was not there–Let
the situation be at its worst, that the remedy may appear more clearly. To the intent ye may believe–To inspire
belief is the purpose in Jesus' mind. In the grave four days–No question that he is dead, beyond human help.
Jesus Is the Resurrection
John 11:18-37 When Jesus came, Martha met Him outside the village. There is faith and also a tone of
rebuke in her words–Lord, if thou hadst been here, my brother had not died. She questioned in her mind
why He hadn't come immediately. But I know, that even now . . . She thought this a harder case than illness,
but had hope in Jesus' ability. Is anything too hard for Him who can do all things? When Jesus told her, Thy
brother shall rise again, she thought He spoke of the future Resurrection.
I am the resurrection, and the life–Jesus Christ holds the power of life. He has even more, He IS life. He
that believeth in me, though he were dead, yet shall he live–life in soul and life in body. Jesus gives life to
both. Both are resurrections, the soul being made alive spiritually and the body being made alive after death.
Whosoever liveth–is born again, made alive spiritually–and believeth in me–continues joined to Him by
faith–shall never die–the second death, eternal spiritual death cannot touch him (Revelation 20:14). There will
be a resurrection of the body on some distant day, but for everyone who accepts Jesus as Lord and Savior, there
is an immediate resurrection from sin to salvation, from darkness to light, from bondage to freedom, from death
