into a life that is everlasting. Believest thou this? She saith unto him, Yea, Lord. Martha's faith reached far
enough. Her mind may not have comprehended all, but in taking Him in, she took in all He could do and would
do. Jesus wept. At the grave of Lazarus we see Jesus sharing human sorrow. He continues to share it to this
very hour. "Does Jesus care? . . . Oh, yes, He cares, I know He cares, His heart is touched with my grief . . . I
know my Savior cares." Thank God for a caring Jesus!
Lazarus Resurrected
John 11:38-44 Jesus . . . groaning in himself–grieved and burdened. Take ye away the stone. When Jesus
Himself was raised from the dead, angels rolled back the stone from the door of the tomb. But on this occasion Jesus
refused to use divine power so long as there was human power available and unused. He commanded human beings
to roll back the stone. When man is involved, God will give him a part to do. God will not do for us what we can
do for ourselves. Martha thought of the immediate problem–he stinketh. There was a weakness in her faith. Jesus
tried to help it–if thou wouldest believe, thou shouldest see . . . We have many stones to roll aside to get our faith
where it needs to be to receive miracles from God. Some are the stones of unbelief, doubt, and anxiety. Jesus lifted
up his eyes–All His work was in close relationship with His Father. Thou hearest me always–never a break in their
fellowship, nothing to hinder His prayers. This is how WE fulfill the Scripture, "Pray without ceasing" (1
Thessalonians 5:17). Broken fellowship with God brings a hindrance in our prayers. This union with God is the
secret of victory and prayer answers for us as well as for Jesus. Because of the people which stand by I said it.
The concern of Jesus was always for the people around Him. That they may believe that thou hast sent me. Here
we see from Jesus' words how important it is that we believe this–for if ye believe not that I am he, ye shall die
in your sins (John 8:24).
He cried . . . Lazarus, come forth. And he that was dead came forth. By His Word Jesus had power over
death. Lazarus was not raised to life as we will be on the Resurrection Day. He had to die again. Then we all will
be changed and made immortal, to die no more. Christ was the first to experience this change to His body (1
Corinthians 15:20). Loose him, and let him go. Now was complete the purpose for which He had acted as He had.
The faith of the sisters was honored, many believers were added, the disciples were anchored stronger in faith, and
God and His Son were glorified. Lazarus was bound with graveclothes, and his face was bound about with a napkin
when he came forth. Even after men are saved, they need the help of others in order to break many of the binding
powers that sin had placed upon them. It is our duty, as saints, to help to loose them and let them go free.
God's Will
How many of our misfortunes would be for the glory of God if we only let Him finish what He has begun? This
is His plan for giving us blessing. God can use even sickness and death to our good and His glory if we hold onto
Him in faith and let Him follow out His purpose.
JUST A THOUGHT
The promises of God are certain, but they do not
all mature in ninety days.

JESUS ENTERS JERUSALEM
Scripture Text: Matthew 21:1-11
It is Passover time in Jerusalem. Thousands of pilgrims are traveling
to the city for the yearly feast and worship. One among them, Jesus Christ
of Nazareth, has a greater purpose. He is coming to die. The journey to
Jerusalem was almost finished. Jesus and the disciples climbed the slope
of the Mount of Olives. Jesus knew a donkey and her colt were tied in
Bethany, and He sent two disciples to bring them. They were not proud
horses of war but lowly donkeys of peace and service. This was a fulfillment of prophecy.
MEMORY VERSE: And if any man say aught unto you, ye shall say, The Lord hath need of them; and
straightway he will send them.
Matthew 21:3
Finding the Colt
Matthew 21:1-3 Coming from Jericho, Jesus and His disciples retreat to the slope of Olivet. Close by is the
village of Bethphage. Two disciples are sent to bring from Bethphage an ass tied, and a colt with her. It was an
unbroken colt whereon never man sat. On this eventful day the Lord had need of something. He, the King of the
universe, had to borrow the colt of a lowly donkey to ride into Jerusalem in triumph. Jesus knew this trip to
Jerusalem meant suffering and death. Let us never think of Him as one who was pursued by His enemies and at last
overtaken and brought to wicked judgment. He faced the tragic facts of life and walked toward them. The only
answer these disciples were to give was The Lord hath need of them. Jesus did not require much from the villager
who owned the animal, but He required what the man had. The Lord today has needs; He needs what WE have.
Nothing is too lowly to be used in His service. Herod had nothing to contribute on that day, neither had the Roman
Emperor. But the humble villager who had a donkey's colt did have something the Lord needed, and he was willing
to give it for the cause of Christ. What might our reaction be if someone walked into our driveway and began to
drive our automobile away and the only reply we received from him was that the Lord had need of it?
Prophecy Fulfilled
Matthew 21:4-9 All this was done, that it might be fulfilled . . . thy King cometh . . . This whole thing was
the fulfillment of Zechariah's prophecy (Zechariah 9:9-10). For this purpose Jesus came into the world. Pomp and
ceremony mark the doings of earthly kings. Here the King of kings advanced to His death. He owned the cattle on
a thousand hills, yet borrowed, not a horse of war, but a lowly donkey of peace and service. It was unbroken, yet
miraculously responded to Jesus' control at a time when the happenings around the animal were such as to cause
it to be completely out of control.
A very great multitude–Many gathered because of the miracles Jesus had performed along the way. They came
from Jerusalem to meet the One who raised the dead and opened the blind eyes. Spread their garments in the
way–branches from the trees–honoring Jesus. The crowds waved palm branches, gathered twigs from the trees, and
made from these and their own garments a carpet over which Jesus could ride. No wonder the donkey stayed calm
through all of this. Here was Heaven's King riding on his back over earth's highways. The Jews had sought to stone
Him, yet He fearlessly let all see Him come. He rides to His death but weeps for His rejecters. He owns all yet

This was unplanned by man but certainly planned by God. He told His prophets of it hundreds of years before.
Fulfillment of prophecy is proof of the truth of the Bible and of the deity of Christ. Without seeing and beforehand,
Jesus knew where the colt was and what would be done and said. Superhuman knowledge and mastery over nature
are honors belonging to God. These are signs of deity.
Not All Joy
Matthew 21:10-11 And when he was come into Jerusalem, all the city was moved–Josephus estimates two
and one-half million to have attended the Passover. A great multitude, indeed, witnessed this great event in history.
In the midst of the joy was grief. Jesus was grieving that although He came to save all, not all would be saved.
Luke tells us that Jesus beheld the city, and wept over it, Saying, If thou hadst known . . . the things which
belong unto thy peace! There, laid out before Him was a city, beyond it a nation, and beyond that a world so
blinded by sin as to refuse the thing it needed most. This, not His own coming suffering and death, brought tears
from the heart of Jesus.
God was ready to give to the world what the people had waited for and longed for during centuries, namely, the
Messiah and His kingdom. But these foolish ones only looked around and in cold indifference, as the Messiah came
into the city, asked, "Who is this?" No doubt, many of these ones who cried Hosanna to the son of David at this
hour, would cry, Crucify him in just a few days. Jesus is the King of the universe. Dear one, is He your King? And
the multitude said, This is Jesus the prophet of Nazareth of Galilee. Here was their King, the Son of God, and
when they were asked, they did not have the correct answer to give. They thought He was a mere prophet. A
greater than a prophet was here, but these people, even after He had done such great works, did not recognize
Him as Who He really was. What would your answer be?
JUST A THOUGHT
We cannot all play the same instrument, but
we can all be in the same key.

JESUS NEARING HIS DEATH
Scripture Text: Mark 14:10-11, 18-21, 27-43
Jesus foresaw His death and knew it would be hard for the disciples to understand. Though
it was a time of great distress for Him, He did not forget to show them the real meaning of His
suffering. Judas was chosen by Jesus to be one of the twelve disciples. He was in the very
presence of Jesus, physically, yet he separated from Him spiritually. Why? What happened in
between that made him seek a way to betray Jesus to His enemies? Did he fail to watch and
pray? Did he allow evil thoughts and desires to come and remain in his heart? Let us see what
God's eternal Word has to say about the answers to these questions. Compare with Matthew
MEMORY VERSE: . . . O my Father, if it be possible, let this cup pass from me:
nevertheless not as I will, but as thou wilt.
Matthew 26:39
The Sinful Plot
Mark 14:10-11 And Judas Iscariot, one of the twelve . . . Judas was chosen by Jesus to preach the Gospel.
He was given power over unclean spirits and to heal disease. Went unto the chief priests to betray Him unto them.
The priests wanted revenge. They allowed a spirit of resentment to work in their hearts and cause them to murder
Jesus. Judas failed to watch and pray, as many do today, and allowed the spirit of greed to place the love of money
before his love for Jesus. Both being evil, they bargained together to do evil. When we have a spirit that desires to
betray Jesus, the enemy will make it convenient to do so.
Mark 14:18-21 One of you . . . shall betray me. This was a most serious moment in the life of Judas. He was
about to be turned over to Satan, but Jesus, by naming him out, offered him one last opportunity to repent. Judas
failed in his time of visitation. How about you, dear one? Judas had to suffer the consequences of his decision. So
will each of us. Judas went out and it was night (John 13:30). When one turns from Jesus, He always goes into
darkness.
It Is Possible to Fall
Mark 14:27-31 Walking from Jerusalem to Gethsemane, Jesus said, All ye shall be offended–all the disciples
would be turned aside from Him. A lack of spiritual power and weakness in the flesh would cause this. Fear and
bewildered disappointment would cause all of the disciples to be offended because of Jesus. Peter would even deny
Him. Jesus quoted the prophecy which He was fulfilling (Zechariah 13:7). But he spake . . . I will not deny thee . . .
Likewise also said they all. Each man thought he was strong in himself. Jesus tried to help them to see and
understand their weakness in themselves (1 Corinthians 10:11-12; 1 Peter 5:8-9).
Gethsemane
Mark 14:32-36 And they came to . . . Gethsemane . . . Sit ye here, while I shall pray. In Gethsemane Jesus
left eight disciples waiting and went farther on with Peter, James, and John. Then He left them to wait and watch
and went yet farther on to pray. Jesus needed their friendship. A terrific battle was raging in His heart, right against

wrong, God against Satan, the flesh against the spirit. His human nature and His divine nature were in a life-and-
death struggle on which depended the salvation of lost mankind. The eternal fate of all the world was held in Jesus'
hands. In this greatest battle and greatest victory that the world has ever known, all the powers of Satan and hell

The thing coming to pass was greater than He had expected. My soul is exceeding sorrowful unto death . . .
If possible take away this cup. The terror He faced here was not a concern with the probability of physical pain.
It was not of the body nor of the mind, but of the soul. Nevertheless not what I will, but what thou wilt. By
keeping His trust in His Father, by submitting fully to Him, by deciding to carry out the plan they together had made,
this great victory was won. It was the will of the Heavenly Father that Jesus suffer and die. There in prayer, alone,
Jesus won the victory for all time. On Calvary He only carried it out. Jesus received no as an answer to His prayer
that if it were possible this cup would be taken away. No is sometimes God's will. To seek and accept God's will
is real prayer.
The Flesh Is Weak
Mark 14:37-43 And he cometh, and findeth them sleeping . . . couldest not thou watch one hour? What
a small favor to ask one who had made such broad statements earlier. Lip service only. How much might the
disciples have learned if they had stayed awake, watched, and prayed with Jesus! Watch ye and pray, lest ye enter
into temptation–this is the only way through which temptation loses its power. When Jesus said to Peter, the flesh
is weak, He could speak from His own present experience with that flesh. Because He knows and conquered it, He
is able to make us conquerors also (Hebrews 2:18).
The problem of suffering is one of the most difficult with which Christianity has to deal. The suffering of the
saints and of those who live holy, blameless lives remains as a bewildering issue to the human race. Atheism and
unbelievers have never come up with any satisfactory answer. Christianity faces the problem firmly because of the
fact that Jesus Himself suffered. It is a part of God's will and plan that His followers suffer for His cause (1 Peter
2:21; 4:1; 2 Timothy 2:12). We must heed His warning through God's Word. Jesus knows all the ways that we are
weak. He will give us strength to endure to the end. As we try to flee from trouble because it is painful, we miss the
spiritual structure it is designed to work in us.
JUST A THOUGHT
People seem to be able to stand adversity
but not prosperity.

JESUS BEFORE THE HIGH PRIEST
Scripture Text: Mark 14:43-72
It is good to compare this Scripture reading with Matthew 26:47-75.
Jesus and eleven of the disciples were in the Garden of Gethsemane.
Jesus had prayed, gained the victory over His fleshly nature, and made
the final decision to suffer for the sins of the world. The high priest
asked Jesus, Art thou the Christ, the Son of the Blessed? In Matthew
22:42 Jesus asked, What think ye of Christ, whose son is he? If His
Father was God, then Christ is God. This is the vital point in all of His work and teaching. This is where He received
His authority and power to do what He claimed. The charge against Jesus was false. This is still a vital point to each
of us. Read Isaiah, Chapter 53.
MEMORY VERSE: Yea, mine own familiar friend, in whom I trusted, which did eat of my bread, hath lifted up
his heel against me.
Psalm 41:9
Judas Betrays Jesus
Mark 14:43-46 Judas had gone from the upper room to meet Christ's enemies and to carry out their evil plan.
Now he came bringing a large mob with swords and staves. Judas, now demon-possessed and forgetting that Jesus
sees hearts (how quickly one forgets the truth he has learned when he leaves Christ and sells out to the world),
pointed Jesus out to the mob by kissing Him. This was false and hypocritical. Master, master–but Jesus was no
longer his master; he had cast off His rule. The religious leaders had sent this rough mob. To what depths religionists
can sink when they turn down Jesus in their inward spirit and emphasize outward form (Matthew 26:47-50). When
Jesus acknowledged His identity, all the men went backward, and fell to the ground (John 18:5-6). This alone
should have been proof to all that He was God, but it was not. Sin blinds. They . . . took him.
Peter's Defense
Mark 14:47-52 The disciples were startled at what they saw. Impulsive Peter, forgetting all Jesus had taught
them about Christian weapons, struck with his sword and cut off the ear of one of the high priest's servants. Jesus
immediately healed it–once again a show of miracle power and love that should have turned His enemies into
friends, but did not (Luke 22:51). Jesus, calling attention to the cowardice of taking Him like this, forbade further
resistance. Put up again thy sword . . . (Matthew 26:52). This was God's will. He must accept the suffering. And
they all forsook him, and fled. This was fulfillment of Scripture (Matthew 26:54-56).
Jesus Falsely Accused

court of the Jews. Peter followed him afar off–a most dangerous place to be found. This is one of the first steps
to backsliding. Council sought for witness against Jesus . . . found none. Witnesses were necessary. Many were

Jesus Condemned
Mark 14:60-65 The high priest stood up–no doubt angered by failure–and asked the reason for Jesus' silence.
Then, Art thou the Christ, the Son of the Blessed? The name of God, the sacred office of the high priest, and the

He realized that he had taken hold of a problem much too large for him to handle. But for a high priest to rend his
clothes was against God's law (Leviticus 21:10). Caiaphas quickly judged Jesus guilty of blasphemy for His claim.
All condemned him to be guilty of death. Without any attempt to investigate the truth of Jesus' claim, Caiaphas

They were so contemptible as to spit upon, strike, and blaspheme Him. His captors mockingly challenged Him to

highest religious leaders of the nation! The charges against Him were false. He was the Son of God and had
authority to do what He claimed. This is still the vital point to each of us. Whom do you accept Him to be? (John
8:24). Violence is always the tool of an evil cause. What tools can a righteous cause depend upon? Truth, reason,
justice, investigation, patience, and trust in God. This an evil cause cannot do. One tool used by the enemy in our
day is the use of terms such as "extremist," "fanatic," or "narrow-minded." They attempt to throw a scare into the
camp of the saints. Jesus' trial was unjust, but a just one could never have condemned Him (Matthew 26:53, 54).
Peter's Denial
Mark 14:66-72 And as Peter was beneath . . . warming himself at the enemies' fire. Just a short time ago
Peter was following afar off. Now we find him warming at the enemies' fire. Oh, how quickly the enemy of
our souls can pull us down! These final verses allow us to see how some small thing can quickly bring us down

of those away from God who were deep in sin. He began to curse and to swear, saying, I know not this
man . . . He lied about his friendship with Jesus.
Friend, is this great Savior yours? Are you ashamed of Him?
JUST A THOUGHT
The harder the fall, the higher the bounce–if you
are made of the right material.

JESUS TRIED AND CRUCIFIED
Scripture Text: Mark 15:1-39
In this lesson today we once again relate to the happening in history that
is so great it is beyond our comprehension, and yet so simple that even
children may understand when told how great God's love is for all mankind.
The few hours between Christ's victory in Gethsemane and this lesson's
events held the trial of Jesus, the denial of Peter, the release of Barabbas,
and the cruel actions by the soldiers. Jesus' acceptance of it all showed
more strength than to have fought back. No fault was found in Jesus. It was
sin that crucified Him, your sin and mine. Jesus took our place. It takes love
to die for good people, but greater love to die for sinners and enemies.
All three courts where Jesus appeared allowed their Prisoner to be
abused contrary to their laws. What faces a land whose courts become
corrupted?
MEMORY VERSE:
But God commendeth his love toward us, in that, while we were yet sinners, Christ
died for us.
Romans 5:8
Jesus Condemned
Mark 15:1-21 In the morning . . . bound Jesus . . . delivered him to Pilate, the Roman governor. It had
been night when Caiaphas and his court tried Jesus and condemned Him to death. Therefore, in the morning,
the group went to Pilate, accused Jesus, and asked for His death. Jesus gave no answer, even though Jewish law
had no authority to put Him to death. Pilate marvelled that Jesus answered nothing. Because Jesus was a
Galilean, Pilate sent Him to King Herod who found no reason to condemn Him and, after mocking Him, sent
Him back (Luke 23:6-11). Pilate found no fault in Jesus and desired to release Him. His human thinking led
him to believe that the people would rather have Jesus released than Barabbas. How wrong he was! Release
Barabbas . . . Crucify . . . the King of the Jews. The people, led by the chief religious persons of the land,
clamored for Jesus to die. They chose Barabbas instead of Jesus to be released at the Passover time. Is the world
much different in their choice in our day? Pilate yielded, scourged Jesus, and gave Him to be crucified. Pilate
was deceived in his heart to believe that a pan of water could wash away the guilt of his action (Matthew 27:24).
The soldiers considered the Prisoner fair prey for their degenerate "fun." They used a purple robe, crown
of thorns, and a reed to ridicule His claim to being King. They saluted and bowed in fun. They insulted, spit
upon, and struck Him. Through it all, Jesus made no resistance. Then they led him out to crucify him.

his garments–the soldiers divided His clothes (Psalm 22:18). Crucifixion meant the worst of human savagery
inflicting the most intense human suffering. THE KING OF THE JEWS–did Pilate believe it true? (See John

way to God (Hebrews 10:19-20). A hand from Heaven did it. Those looking on knew these were no ordinary events.
No longer was man held off from God with a priest representing him once a year. Now each saint is a priest, free
to come all the way to God through the Holy Spirit's indwelling. If you do not have this experience, it is waiting for
you. To the Christian, death is not a dead-end street; it is a triumphal door through which he may pass on to the joys
of an eternal home. Truly this man was the Son of God–the centurion believed.

Human nature has not improved so very much since the
day of the Cross. Shameful motives still cause
men to crucify our Lord afresh daily.

JESUS' RESURRECTION
Scripture Texts: Matthew 28:1-10; 1 Corinthians 15:20-21
Christ's Resurrection is the completion of the plan that He came to establish
by dying. Without the Resurrection all would have been ended and lost. It is the
greatest of all miracles. The Resurrection stands joined with the Crucifixion at
the highest point of history. The day following the Crucifixion was of the
darkest the world has ever known.
It is a blow to any group to have their leader taken from them by death. But
with the message of the Resurrection, the brokenhearted jumped up and faced a
new day with glad hearts. Christ crucified and risen again was the main burden of
the Apostles' preaching. Jesus never spoke of His approaching Crucifixion without
speaking, also, of His Resurrection.
MEMORY VERSE: Yet a little while, and the world seeth me no more; but ye see me: because I live, ye shall
live also.
John 14:19
Faithfulness Paid Off
When Jesus died, Joseph of Arimathaea and Nicodemus buried Jesus in Joseph's new tomb as believing women
stood nearby. Pilate, sick and tired of the whole affair, wearily consented to the sealing of the tomb.
Matthew 28:1-4 In the end of the sabbath, as it began to dawn toward the first day of the week–before
daybreak on Sunday. The women brought spices and ointments for the body of Jesus. Great earthquake–earth and
Heaven alike were being shaken. A great turning point in history had arrived. Nature sounded out the event even
as when Jesus died. The cause of this earthquake is told–for the angel of the Lord descended. Here was God
Himself, His angels, and His people working in unity and harmony in His plan for all of His kingdom together.
Rolled back the stone–man had sealed it. Sat upon it–symbolic of Heaven's contempt for man's power and estimate
of events. Man's rules cannot hinder God's plan. His countenance was like lightning, and his raiment white as
snow–reminding of Jesus' transfiguration. Keepers did shake–those guarding against the stealing of Jesus' body
were frightened. Fear is one of mankind's greatest enemies. Faith is the only cure for fear. Not faith in ourselves,
not faith in anything the world can offer, but faith in Jesus, who had been crucified, but now was raised from the
dead and glorified. The removing of the stone had nothing to do with Christ's coming out of the tomb. It was only
so the people could see the empty tomb.
Matthew 28:5-7 Angel . . . said . . . Fear not ye . . . He is not here–He did not belong here among the dead.
He is life; He could not stay. The dark, dead tomb could not hold life and light, Jesus Christ. Thank God! He is now
Savior of all the world. All the power of Satan could not hold Him there. He is risen, as he said–told them plainly,
recalled Jesus' own words. Now they understood what before they did not. Come, see the place–no concealment.
God wanted them to have proof. Truth can afford to lay bare the facts. The angels (Luke 24:4 tells of two) stayed
to send the women with word to the disciples. Go quickly, and tell . . . he is risen from the dead . . . he goeth
before you into Galilee. God wanted the facts of the Resurrection known. The command was GO and TELL. This
is still the command to Christian believers concerning the good news of a living Christ. Christianity is a missionary
religion. They were to meet Him at some point in Galilee. We have definite appointments with Him–our daily

devotions, the carrying of His righteousness in our everyday lives to others, attendance to church services of

Jesus Met Them

men who had forsaken Him when He needed them most, even denied Him. He in His moment of greatest triumph,
called them my brethren. That they go into Galilee, and there shall they see me. What great anticipation this
must have stirred within the hearts of these brethren! They did see Him there.
Christ, the Firstfruits
First Corinthians 15:20 Now is Christ risen–it is sure–and become the firstfruits–He was the first to have

Jesus actually arose in body. If not, He did not arise at all. Jesus' resurrection is the guarantee of ours. He said,
Because I live, ye shall live also (John 14:19). When we arise, we will have bodies. Jesus did, and we shall be like

with evil is one of them.

JESUS APPEARS AFTER RESURRECTION

Following His Resurrection Jesus was not with His disciples constantly as before. His
body seemed freed from the limitations of space and matter in ways not described. He
appeared and vanished suddenly, passing through closed doors. Yet He was the same loving
Jesus as always. The main portion of His work was completed when He arose. He remained
forty days to give proof of His Resurrection, to comfort and settle His disciples after the
shattering experience of the Crucifixion, and to give final teaching and instructions for the
spread of the Gospel. Very important to us are these instructions, for they rest on our lives
to carry out. The close of each Gospel Book records them.
The disciples had abundant proof of the Resurrection of Jesus in the many appearances
of Him to them. We study some today.

And they said one to another, Did not our heart burn within us, while he talked with us by
the way, and while he opened to us the scriptures?
Luke 24:32
Evening After Resurrection
John 20:19-20 The same day at evening–the day He arose. Luke 24:13-32 tells us of Jesus meeting two
disciples earlier in the day on the road to Emmaus. The doors were shut where the disciples were assembled for
fear of the Jews–fear that the recent violence to Jesus might fall on them. They were a marked people. Is not it yet
so in our day? Came Jesus–the shut doors did not hinder Him. Peace be unto you–the same loving Jesus bringing
peace to troubled hearts. They needed His peace, and we need it too. (Luke 24:33-40 tells of the same appearing.)
Shewed . . . his hands and his side–His wounds proved that it was Jesus. Also, that He had come through death
with the same body.
John 20:24-25 Thomas . . . said . . . Except I shall see . . . and put . . . and thrust . . . I will not believe--
Thomas had to be shown.
One Week Later
John 20:26-29 After eight days–a little more than a week later. Again Jesus came through shut doors and
appeared with the same greeting as before. Thomas was with them this time. Saith he to Thomas, Reach hither
thy finger–He knew Thomas' unbelief and what he had said. He gave the proof he asked. Be not faithless, but
believing. He was not pleased with Thomas' doubt. The sin of unbelief locks out all of God's graces. All His stay
here Jesus had to urge people to believe. Now at its close, He still has to. We are prone, like Thomas, to doubt unless
we see, and sometimes after we see. This grieves God. Faith is that arm by which we reach and take hold of God
and His blessings. We must have faith. Jesus sets no limits to the possibilities of faith. Why should we? He said,
". . . all things are possible to him that believeth" (Mark 9:23).
Thomas answered . . . My Lord and my God. Immediately his faith took hold in Jesus, and he knew Him as
God. Because thou hast seen me, thou hast believed–this is better than a stubborn spirit of unbelief which will
not believe even though it sees. But better yet, is the childlike faith that believes without seeing. Jesus called such
blessed.

At the Seashore
John 21:1-11 At the sea of Tiberias–same as Galilee. The disciples had gone to Galilee as He had said
(Matthew 28:10). Seven are together. Peter saith unto them, I go a fishing–confused and uncertain, he turned to
his old life. Caught nothing–the old life is never the same when turning back to it after living with Jesus. God

miracle.

John 21:12-14 Come and dine–inviting them to eat with Him. Taketh bread, and giveth them, and fish
likewise. The Master, victorious over all things, still desiring to serve others. None . . . durst ask . . . knowing . . .

failures caused them to be estranged. Failure to do right always brings a strangeness to our relationship with Jesus.
Third time that Jesus shewed himself–that is, to a group of the eleven. Ten definite appearances are mentioned,

Anything which separates children of God is

JESUS' ASCENSION
Scripture Texts: Acts 1:1-12; John 14:3
Jesus showed Himself alive after His passion by many proofs. To the Jews,
Jesus is a martyr who died for a great cause two thousand years ago. But He is set
forth in the New Testament as more than a martyr. God raised Him from the dead,
and He is a glorified and risen Savior. He returned from the grave to be with His
disciples for a period of forty days, appearing to them time and again during this
time.
Jesus' leaving of the world was as unique as the rest of His life. It was a
miracle. His death was not the end. The Resurrection was not all. His ascension
out of the world was not the end. Every step but leads on to the next one. Today
we look at what the Scripture tells of His ascension.
MEMORY VERSE: And if I go and prepare a place for you, I will come again, and receive you unto myself; that
where I am, there ye may be also.

Seen Forty Days
Acts 1:1-3 The former treatise–a written composition on a particular subject. The same writer wrote the Book
of Luke for the same friend, Theophilus. In the Book of Luke he had given Christ's doings and teachings until His
Ascension–the day in which he was taken up. In Acts he tells of the Ascension more fully and goes on with the
history of the church immediately following. After that he (Jesus) through the Holy Ghost had given
commandments–He and the Holy Ghost worked together, as well as with the Father. To whom–to the Apostles–he
shewed himself alive . . . by many infallible proofs . . . forty days–we have studied some of these proofs.
Stay at Jerusalem
Acts 1:4-5 Assembled together . . . commanded . . . not depart from Jerusalem–without His command they
probably would have returned to Galilee. The Resurrection had changed the mood of the disciples from despair to
joy. But there was uncertainty as to what they were expected to do, and they were reluctant to take the first step,
whatever it might be. Jesus settled this by charging them not to depart from Jerusalem, but wait for the promise
of the Father. What promise? Read Luke 24:49–Ye be endued with power from on high–a promise of power from
God for the great work ahead of them. John truly baptized with water; but ye shall be baptized with the Holy
Ghost . . . This promise was about to be fulfilled.
Acts 1:6-8 They asked . . . wilt thou at this time restore . . . the kingdom . . . ? Israel was under the foreign
rule of Rome. The disciples had a mistaken idea that Jesus' mission was to win independence for Israel. It is not
for you to know . . . They did not understand, as yet, the real nature of Christ's kingdom. Holy Spirit baptism would
give them understanding. But ye shall receive power–not political power but spiritual–after that the Holy Ghost
is come upon you: and ye shall be witnesses–He turned their eyes toward their true life's work. Unto me both in
Jerusalem (at home), and in all Judaea (next door), and in Samaria (home missions), and unto the uttermost
part of the earth (foreign missions).
Here is one of the great verses of the Bible. It makes very plain that any spiritual success we gain depends upon

our having received God's gift of the Holy Spirit. Intelligence is not enough. Great effort is not enough. Nothing is

Acts 1:9-11 While they beheld–in plain view, not secret–he was taken up–the law of gravity lost its effect,
He ascended in the air–a cloud received him. He went into or beyond a cloud, similar to the way the saints will go

stedfastly–in rapt attention, wonder, and expectation. Two men stood by them–so absorbed in watching Jesus they
had not seen them come. In white apparel–their clothing and their message identified them as angels. Which also
said . . . this same Jesus . . . shall so come–they were told what to expect. In like manner as ye have seen him
go–He will come in the clouds. It will not be secret. Every eye shall see him (Matthew 24:30; 1 Thessalonians
4:16,17; Revelation 1:7). It was necessary that Jesus go away. Why?
Obeyed Christ's Command
Acts 1:12 Returned . . . unto Jerusalem–in obedience to His command–from the mount called Olivet. The
disciples returned to Jerusalem, not forsaken and forlorn, but with a living hope of seeing Him again and a definite
goal of waiting for the baptism of the Holy Ghost. Jesus had told them where to go, how long to stay, what to look
for, and what to expect.
John 14:3 If I go and prepare a place for you–He promised to do this–I will come again, and receive you
unto myself; that where I am–in Heaven–ye may be also. What a bright hope this is! The disciples did what they
were told to do, and they did it without murmuring. They went where they were told to go. They waited, no doubt

What a place mountains occupy in our Lord's ministry! On a mount, He preached His most famous sermon. On
a mountain, He was transfigured. On a hill called Golgotha, He was crucified. On a mountain, He appeared to His
disciples after He arose. And from the side of a mountain, He ascended into His eternal glory!

happens to a wagon if one wheel comes off.

JESUS APPEARS TO STEPHEN
Scripture Texts: Acts 6:8-15; Acts 7:51-60
Stephen's vision of Jesus was evidence that Jesus still lived as much as
ever, and that He went to Heaven from the earth. The church knew this by
faith in His Word, by the works He continued to do through them, and by the
Presence of the Holy Spirit Whom He had promised to send. This sight of
Him, as studied in today's lesson, was added evidence to them and to us. The
whole history of the church is one long proof that Jesus lives. A few times,
He gave added proof in a visible appearance. We study one today, that of His
appearance to Stephen, the first person in the Church of God to wear the
crown of martyrdom. Witnessing to the truth has in all ages raised
opposition. Stephen summoned his generation to new spiritual heights.
MEMORY VERSE: And said, Behold, I see the heavens opened, and the Son of man standing on the right hand
of God.
Acts 7:56
A Faithful New Witness
We read in Acts 6:1 that when the number of the disciples was multiplied, there arose a murmuring . . .
Murmuring concerning others' success always leads to trouble. Certain of the Greek-speaking Jews believed that
their widows were being neglected in the distribution of food and other necessities in favor of the widows of other
Jews. The Apostles brought the matter before the whole church and asked them to seek out seven men who were
full of the Holy Ghost and wisdom, and put them in charge of this affair.
Acts 6:8-11 And Stephen–a Greek-speaking Jew, one of the seven chosen for this special work of distributing
food to the needy, made this an opportunity to do a great spiritual service. The name Stephen means "crown." Full
of faith and power, did great wonders and miracles--a true and active saint. He had power because the Holy
Ghost had come upon him (verse 5). Then there arose Greek-speaking Jews–disputing with Stephen. They still
were not satisfied. This kind of spirit in people cannot be satisfied by attempting to appease it. Active, successful
work for the Lord always brings opposition. And they were not able to resist the wisdom and the spirit by which
he spake. When his opponents were not able to withstand his wisdom, their thoughts turned to violence. Suborned
men–procured privately or unlawfully and bribed them to twist the words of Stephen. They claimed that they had
heard him speak blasphemous words against Moses, and against God, which indicates that these men put Moses
and God on the same level. This was true blasphemy.
Stephen Before the Council
Acts 6:12-15 They stirred up the people . . . caught him, and brought him to the council–to the Sanhedrin.
False witnesses–they twisted what had been said about the temple and the Law, Jesus' words about the temple of
His body (John 2:19-21), and the relation of the Gospel to the Law. Only the Holy Spirit can reveal these things,

When the high priest asked if these things were so, Stephen took the opportunity to preach a sermon by recounting
the history of Israel to show (1) that the favor and worship of God are not confined to places, as the temple, and (2)

The Council Before Stephen
Acts 7:51-54 Stephen ended his sermon with a direct accusation–Ye stiffnecked and uncircumcised–stubborn

Stephen's Spirit

Let us consider the similarity of Stephen's death with that of Jesus. Stephen was condemned by the council as

enemies; the Words on the lips of Jesus were for the forgiveness of His murderers.
Stephen had a brief career. He preached but one sermon. But his soul burned as a fiery furnace for the cause of
his Lord. Are you willing to suffer for your devotion to the Lord Jesus?

Saul's Character and Zeal
Acts 9:1-2 Saul, yet breathing out threatenings and slaughter against the disciples of the Lord–so full of

Syrian city located 150 miles away. This indicated the unmercifulness of Saul's zeal.

Acts 9:3-9 Suddenly there shined round about him–it came suddenly–a light from heaven–over him from
above. It was about noon, and the light was above the brightness of the sun. No doubt, this was the same light which
had shown on the face of Moses and later was seen in the transfiguration. It blinded Saul. Fell to the
earth–powerless–a voice . . . Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me? Jesus and His people are so closely united that

they persecute Christ. Who art thou, Lord?–knew it was One greater than himself. I am Jesus–he saw Jesus and

religion. I verily thought with myself, that I ought to do many things contrary to the name of Jesus (Acts 26:9).
Hard for thee to kick against the pricks–as an ox kicking back against the goad would but injure itself. Saul was

Trembling and astonished–greatly affected by fear and astonishment–Lord, what wilt thou have me to
do?–complete surrender, no conditions. This was the turning point in Saul's life. It was here that he turned from

making it an opportunity for both the giver and receiver to have a blessing. The men . . . with him . . . speechless,
hearing a voice . . . seeing no man–they heard the voice but did not understand the Words. Saul only, saw Jesus
and understood the Words. (Read Acts 26:13-15.) Saul arose . . . saw no man–blind–led him by the hand . . . The
one who led others, bound, to prison, is now being led to Damascus.
The Street Called Straight
Acts 9:10-16 And the Lord said . . . go into the street . . . called Straight, and enquire in the house of Judas
for . . . Saul. Ananias was in shape spiritually for the Lord to use him. The directions are given in detail. Nothing
is left to chance. Ananias knew exactly what he was supposed to do. For, behold, he prayeth. Saul, being a
Pharisee, had said many prayers; now he was praying. He was praying in the right spirit and for the right cause. God
was preparing Saul to receive Ananias and preparing Ananias to go to Saul. When God sends us, He prepares the
way before us. Ananias knew all about Saul, how he had persecuted the Christians even unto death. Nothing short
of a vision from God would have motivated Ananias to go and call upon Saul. The Lord said unto him, Go . . .
he is a chosen vessel unto me. God chooses the best. To bear my name before the Gentiles . . . Saul was to be
an apostle first to the Gentiles. He stood before Gentile kings, and many Jews were saved under his ministry also.
Saul Received Sight
Acts 9:17-20 Ananias went–he believed and obeyed. Putting his hands on him, said, Brother Saul–Blessed
title! He was a brother now, born into the family of God. Jesus . . . hath sent me, that thou mightest receive thy
sight–physical sight–and be filled with the Holy Ghost–spiritual sight, the Holy Spirit would lead and direct him
from now on. Immediately . . . fell . . . scales . . . he received sight . . . arose . . . baptized–no hesitation. Saved
people want to obey. Straightway he preached Christ . . . that he is the Son of God. Saul had just learned this,
and he could not keep it still. It was burning in his soul.
When Was Saul Saved?
Who can know for certain when Saul was saved? Salvation is a change from a condition of danger to one of
safety, a transfer from the power of darkness to the kingdom of his dear Son, from serving Satan to serving God,
from death in sin to life in Christ. Between the time Saul fell to the earth and when he arose from the earth a
mighty change took place. He fell in rebellion against Jesus; he rose submitted to Him. He fell an unbeliever; he
rose a believer. He fell a persecutor; he rose to pray. Saul received his sight. Have you received yours?
JUST A THOUGHT
A church membership does not make one a Christian
any more than owning a piano makes
one a musician.

JESUS APPEARS TO JOHN
Scripture Text: Revelation 1:9-18
The Apostle John, toward the end of his distinguished ministry, suffered
persecution at the hands of the Roman emperor, Domitian, about A.D. 95. He
had long been pastor of the church in Ephesus and the man of God to whom
the churches in Asia looked as their leader. It was to be expected that a man
of his standing, the last surviving Apostle of the original twelve, should have
felt upon himself the heavy hand of Roman cruelty. He was sent to the Isle of
Patmos, a small island in the Aegean Sea, a short distance from Ephesus. He
speaks of himself as a brother and partaker with the other disciples in the
tribulation and kingdom and patience which are in Jesus.
Evidences multiply of Christ's resurrection and His continued life in Heaven. Now we look at His appearance
to John.
MEMORY VERSE: I am he that liveth, and was dead; and, behold, I am alive for evermore, Amen.
Revelation 1:18
Our Brother and Companion
Revelation 1:9 I John–the Apostle–brother . . . companion in tribulation–he was just like us, human, suffered
the same trials and limitations as we, also was persecuted. We may tend to feel that Bible characters were so far
above us that God could do for them things He will not do for us. This is not true. They all had the same limitations
and temptations, the same danger of falling as we. And we have the same promises, the same spiritual provisions,
the same access to God as they. In the kingdom and patience of Jesus Christ–had the same place in Christ's
kingdom, the same hope in Him that all Christians have.
Let us examine these three things. Tribulation means suffering of a variety which cleanses the soul and makes
it better. The tribulum, from which this word is derived, was the flail that separated the wheat from the chaff.
Suffering makes many people bitter; when rightly endured–especially when endured in Christian faith–it makes men
better. The kingdom or the rule of God was something which John shared with his brethren. They had that joyful
hold on living reality which enabled them to live in peace and confidence even amid heavy persecutions. The
patience which is in Jesus is a thing which we need to have–patience with ourselves, patience with others, patience
with God, and patience with what appears to us to be His strange providences (Luke 21:19). In the isle . . .
Patmos–where he had been placed in exile–for the word of God . . . testimony of Jesus Christ–his banishment
was persecution for his faith in and preaching of Christ and the Gospel. After the death of Domitian, John was
returned to Ephesus.
John Hears Jesus
Revelation 1:10-11 In the Spirit–alone, banished, separated from the work and the people he loved,
suffering hardship, still John had a place to go to reach Jesus. He retired into the chamber of his heart where
the Holy Spirit lived. There he could worship, talk with the Lord, sup with Jesus on heavenly food, and feel the
Spirit sweetly fill his heart to overflowing. If we have the Holy Spirit, we, like John, can be in the Spirit and

John Saw Jesus
Revelation 1:12-16 I turned . . . saw seven golden candlesticks . . . are the seven churches (verse 20).
One like unto the Son of man–even in His changed appearance, John recognized Jesus, the One he had known
in the flesh. Head and . . . hairs . . . white as snow . . . eyes . . . as a flame of fire . . . feet . . . as if they
burned in a furnace–purity, richness, strength, omniscience, light and glory. Voice . . . many waters–power
and majesty. All the attributes of God. Here Jesus is dressed in attire to put heat on the church. In his right
hand seven stars–the pastors–of the seven churches. Christ held and guarded them in His hand. Out of his
mouth . . . a sharp twoedged sword–judgment, the word of God (Hebrews 4:12). Countenance . . . as the

John's Response
Revelation 1:17 I fell at his feet as dead–all strength gone, overwhelmed, a mere man before the great
God. Submission and worship were so complete that there was an emptying out of all of John's being. He laid his
right hand upon me–the same hand which held the ministers of the churches. Fear not–the same Fear not He so
often used. It is no wonder John was fearful! This was a large responsibility being put on him. I am the first and
the last–trust Me, John. I am the beginning, the ending, and everything in between. I fill all time and am eternal.
Jesus Alive Forevermore
Revelation 1:18 I am he that liveth–He IS life (John 14:6). He has life in Himself (John 5:26)–and was
dead–He is the One John saw die on the Cross. While Jesus speaks of His life in the present and future tense, He
speaks of His death only in the past. He is no longer on the Cross or in the grave. The crucifix (Christ fixed on the
Cross) has no place in Christianity. Behold, I am alive for evermore–He can never be sacrificed again (Romans
6:9). He was offered once for all (Hebrews 10:10-14). We have a living Savior who cannot die again. Amen–it is
sure, certain, true. So be it–the seal of certainty. Have the keys of hell and of death–Jesus has power over these.
He will finally cast them both into the lake of fire (Revelation 20:14). This can be no other than Jesus! Oh, the love,
the mercy, the gentle compassion of Jesus!
JUST A THOUGHT
A church that has to be supported by tea parties, ice cream socials, and fried
chicken dinners is as weak as the tea, as cold as the ice cream, and as dead as the
chicken.

JESUS IN THE FUTURE
Scripture Texts: Matthew 16:27; 24:27; 25:31-33; Revelation 1:7; 1 Thessalonians 4:14-18;
Revelation 19:7
We have looked at Jesus coming from past eternity, living on earth a brief time to redeem
men, and now back home in Heaven with His Father for future eternity. We cannot study the
end of His life. There is no end or "last" of Jesus Christ. Praise God! He lives on forever. Jesus
does not want His people to only look back upon Him in the past. He has told us what to expect in the future.
God's whole program is one. There is unity in everything He does. ALL the saints will be taken together. Enoch
and Abraham will be there, Peter, Paul, all down to the last one saved. There is no language to describe the glorious
scene, all gathered together to see Jesus.
MEMORY VERSE: Therefore let us not sleep as do others; but let us watch and be sober.
1 Thessalonians 5:6
Christ's Second Coming
Matthew 16:27 Son of man shall come–Jesus is coming again–in the glory of his Father–we can only get a
glimpse of this glory at Christ's transfiguration and other biblical scenes–with his angels–the angels have a close
interest and a part in our salvation, yet they never had the privilege of experiencing the joy that salvation brings. In
this event, ALL people will have a very vital interest, for then–at the time of His coming–he shall reward every
man–both good and bad–according to his works–the deeds of our lives determine our judgment.
Matthew 24:27 As the lightning–sudden, for all to see, not secret. This is the way the Second coming of the
Son of man shall be.
The Judgment
Matthew 25:31-33 When the Son . . . shall come in his glory . . . then shall he sit upon the throne–the
Judgment seat of Christ (Romans 14:10-13). The great Savior is now the Judge of all. Before him shall be gathered
all nations–not one person absent–he shall separate . . . sheep from the goats–symbolic of but two kinds of
people. What a sad time for the goats! Do all possible to see them saved before that awful day! The judgment
awaiting each is told in verses 34 and 41. There is more to the end of life than to die; a stern judgment follows
(Hebrews 9:27). Jesus was Savior while He was on earth. At this moment He is our Mediator before the throne of
grace. On the last day He will be our Judge.
Who Are Included?
Revelation 1:7 Behold, he cometh with clouds–as foretold when He ascended (Acts 1:9-11). Every eye shall
see him–it is useless to claim that He has or will come secretly or unknown to even one person. And they also
which pierced him–both the wicked and the saints, dead and alive, will see Him. Thus, the resurrection of all must
precede this. (Read John 5:28-29).
First Thessalonians 4:14 If we believe that Jesus died and rose–just as sure as His death and Resurrection.
Even so–our resurrection hinges on His. Them also which sleep in Jesus will God bring with him–the spirits of

First Thessalonians 4:15-18 We say unto you by the word of the Lord–not Paul's idea but God's Word –We
which are alive and remain–the saints living on earth at the time of Christ's coming–shall not prevent them
which are asleep–the dead saints. The only ones being considered here are saints, dead and alive. He tells us that
the live saints will not go ahead of the dead saints. Lord himself shall descend from heaven with a shout, with
the voice . . . and with the trump–the Voice which will bring them from the graves, heralding the event, calling
forth the dead (1 Corinthians 15:51-52). The dead in Christ shall rise first. Then we which are alive–saints living
at that time–caught up together–all the saints in one great multitude–in the clouds–just as Jesus left, He will be
coming. To meet the Lord in the air: and so shall we ever be with the Lord–go to Heaven to be with Jesus and
His Father forever. Oh! Thank God! For all time and eternity. Comfort one another with these words–testify to
it. We are not told much of Heaven, but just the thought of the hope of attaining it is a comfort in life's trials and
troubles to those of us who are saved from sin.
Note in these verses that our Lord assures us of the inevitability of the Judgment. No one will escape it. Our
whole lives will someday be laid before us by a Judge whose wisdom is perfect, Who has every fact, good and bad
alike before Him, and whose verdict will be set in accordance with the standards of perfect justice. He will make
no mistakes.
The Bridegroom Cometh
Revelation 19:7 Let us be glad and rejoice, and give honour to him–to the Lamb, Jesus Christ–for the
marriage of the Lamb is come–Christ's wedding day. His wife hath made herself ready–the church, ready by
having washed their robes, and made them white in the blood of the Lamb (Revelation 7:14). Jesus will take
His bride to the Heavenly home which He has prepared for her. There they will be together for all eternity. Are you
ready and waiting for the Bridegroom to come? He could come at any time (Matthew 25:13).
This lesson closes this series, but it can find no period to the life of Christ. He is the One which is, and which
was, and which is to come. Praise God! He will come for His bride, judge the world, then continue on as the Ruler,
the Temple, and the Light of Heaven. Beyond that, we know not. That remains yet to be seen. We know it will be
all good and will continue without end.
JUST A THOUGHT
There is no middle ground between good and evil.
